### `discussionboard_channels`

Discussion Board Channels - This implements the requirement for multi-channel/forum environments from the original business requirements (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md Section 2.3, 2.4). 

Channel represents a top-level grouping for boards/forums for both scalability and community segmentation. Maintains 3NF normalization by separating channel metadata from board or topic-specific data. For example, a platform with 'Politics', 'Economics', and 'International Relations' channels allows targeted thread organization and user permissions per channel.

Key relationships: referenced by boards in other domains (not directly here). 
Special behaviors: Disabling a channel hides all associated boards and content without deletion.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique channel identifier.
- `code`: Channel code - Implements unique channel identifier for internal reference. Example: 'POLI', 'ECON'. Ensures normalization by providing atomic lookup field without duplication. Usage: for routing and analytics.
- `name`: Human-readable channel name - Implements user interface representation. Example: 'Politics', 'Economics'. Keeps display values separate from codes for flexibility.
- `description`: Extended channel description - For longer UI help text or onboarding popups. Atomic, nullable for optional UX.
- `enabled`: Channel enabled status - Indicates whether this channel is active and visible to users. Fulfills configurability requirement without hard deletion.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - When the channel was first created. Supports auditability, required for 3NF and not derived.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp - When channel metadata was last changed. Supports audit trails and user interface freshness.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp - Implements business rule: channels never hard-deleted, are flagged for removal. If null, not deleted; if set, should not be shown to users.

### `discussionboard_categories`

Discussion Board Categories - This supports hierarchical topic grouping within channels, directly mapping to the business requirement for organized board structuring from 03_DiscussionBoard_User_Journeys_and_Workflows.md and 04_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md (section 2.3, 2.4). 

Category allows grouping boards for navigational clarity and thematic relevance. Maintains 3NF normalization by atomically storing categories separate from boards or topics. Example: categories like 'International', 'Domestic', 'Elections', under a 'Politics' channel.

Key relationships: often referenced by boards (in other files); can support parent-child via 'parent_id' field if hierarchy is desired.
Special behaviors: Disabling a category hides its boards/topics from users but retains data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique category identifier.
- `discussionboard_channel_id`: Belonged channel's [discussionboard_channels.id](#discussionboard_channels) - Associates the category with its parent channel, ensuring each category is correctly placed in the forum hierarchy. Enforces normalization by separating channel from category business logic.
- `parent_id`: Optional parent category's [discussionboard_categories.id](#discussionboard_categories) - Enables category nesting for themes/subcategories. Null when top-level; fulfills 3NF by storing hierarchy atomically.
- `code`: Category code - Atomic, unambiguous handle for programmatic reference. E.g., 'ELECTIONS'. Maintains normalization and allows unique lookups.
- `name`: Category name - Display string for UI, supports search and multilingual use. Atomic, not derived.
- `description`: Long category description - For help popups, onboarding, or detailed UI. Nullable, kept atomic for 3NF.
- `enabled`: Category enabled state - Fulfills admin business rule for soft-hiding categories without data loss.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - For audit/logging, non-derived.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp - Last metadata modification. Maintains full normalization and is not derived.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp - Category is hidden, not deleted. 3NF compliant, nullable for full retention/audit support.

### `discussionboard_settings`

Discussion Board Global Settings - Implements central configuration management as required in business rules (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md Section 2.6 and 3). 

Allows admin and system-wide settings to be referenced from code and API. All settings are atomic key-value pairs, fully normalized (no pre-calculated aggregates). For example: spam filter thresholds, maintenance modes, global flags. This model is NOT used for user-specific settings (those are in other components).

Key relationships: None (standalone configuration repository).
Special behaviors: Only admin users can modify; changes are logged in the audit records.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique configuration setting row.
- `key`: Setting key - Atomic string, namespaced for collision avoidance. E.g., 'maintenance_mode', 'email:smtp_host'. Fulfills 3NF by logically separating individual settings.
- `value`: Setting value - Actual config data, stored as string for flexibility (booleans stored as 'true'/'false', numbers as strings, etc.). Remains atomic and is not calculated/derived.
- `description`: Description of this setting - Used for admin UI and inline documentation. Nullable for flexibility. Maintains 3NF by separating metadata.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when setting was first added. Fulfills audit/history requirement.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last modification for tracking. Business use: rollback or troubleshooting.

### `discussionboard_audit_logs`

Discussion Board System Audit Trail - Implements mandatory audit logging (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md Section 2.5, 4, 6). 

Captures all system-critical and admin/moderator actions for legal compliance, accountability, and troubleshooting. Maintains 3NF by separating each log entry as an atomic event record. Usage example: records when an admin changes a setting, a moderator deletes content, or a user is suspended. Read-only unless system/admin privilege.

Key relationships: References acting user in other actor components (not handled here).
Special behaviors: Entries are immutable and must not be modified/deleted except by hard data retention policies.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique audit log entry.
- `action`: Audit action description - Atomic, non-derived string classifying the action (e.g., 'SETTING_UPDATE', 'ACCOUNT_SUSPEND'). Fully normalized: each event is one row. Examples: 'BOARD_CREATE', 'POST_DELETE', 'WARNING_ISSUED'.
- `actor_id`: ID of user performing the action - Cross-references actors (members, moderators, admins) in other domains. Fulfills audit traceability requirement by unambiguously linking log to user. This is NOT a foreign key to allow for actor deletion scenarios.
- `target_table`: Target table/entity affected - Describes what system entity was changed (e.g., 'discussionboard_boards', 'discussionboard_threads'). Key for traceability and reporting.
- `target_id`: ID of affected entity - When applicable, stores the row/entity affected by the event. Separate from 'actor_id'. Nullable for actions like login, where there may be no entity affected.
- `details`: Additional details - JSON string or extended data for complex actions (e.g., before/after snapshot). Fully atomic as business rule prohibits redundancy.
- `created_at`: Audit entry creation timestamp - Required, non-derived, for every action (full audit compliance).

### `discussionboard_members`

Member entity for board platform - Implements actor/user identity core from the Actors domain and requirement sections (esp. Role & Registration).  

This models the base member user that can register, post, comment, and interact. Maintains full 3NF normalization—member preferences, authentications, roles, and profile are handled in related tables. Used when linking posts, comments, reports, notifications to a unique user identity.

Example usage: Track who authored a thread, likes a post, or receives a notification.

Key relationships: Links to profiles, authentications, suspensions, moderator/admin entities. 
Special behaviors: Member can only have one unique identity, unique email enforced at authentication level.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each member in the system.
- `joined_at`: Member join date/time - Implements audit/tracking requirement. Indicates when the member registered. Ensures normalization by placing date in member (not profile) for clear audit. E.g. "2025-07-22T11:00:00+09:00".
- `status`: Current member status - Implements business rules on activation/suspension. Values like 'active', 'pending', or 'suspended'. For example, initial status is 'active'; if suspended, some privileges are blocked; status field reflects business logic, not derived from suspension table.

### `discussionboard_moderators`

Moderator entity - Implements moderator elevation from requirements (Role & Permission, Moderation Workflows). 

Stores references to member IDs elevated as moderators. Maintains 3NF as separate table. E.g., a member can have a record here when promoted to moderator; demotion is soft by setting an end timestamp.

Key usage: Map member to moderator privileges, history, and actions.
Key relationships: Links to member, logs actions in discussionboard_moderator_actions.
Special behaviors: Only admins can add records; member cannot be moderator twice at the same time.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Link to the promoted member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Establishes which user is the moderator.
- `promoted_at`: Datetime member became moderator. Implements audit and escalation requirement for privilege history.
- `demoted_at`: Datetime moderator stopped being moderator. Null if currently holds role. Maintains audit trail; 3NF (not in member base table).

### `discussionboard_admins`

Admin entity - Implements admin user architecture per requirements. 

Records which members are elevated to admin status (system superuser). Keeps normalized; not merged with member or moderator. Usage: assign admin API permissions, log system config changes, etc.

Key relationships: FK to member. 
Special: Only unique for each member; admin may also be moderator.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Link to member who is admin. References [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `elevated_at`: Datetime admin privilege granted; implements privilege audit. For example, assigned by platform owner.

### `discussionboard_member_profiles`

Member profile details - Implements requirements for profile management (user journeys, self-editable info, privacy compliance). 

Stores optional extended member info: display name, bio, links, avatar, etc. Strictly 3NF: profile data not mixed with authentication, roles, or business states.

Usage example: Display profile page; allow user edits; fulfill download-my-data requests.

Key relationships: Exists 0 or 1 per member, not required for minimal registration.
Special: All fields optional (nullable = true where privacy applies).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: FK to the owner member. References [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `display_name`: Optional user-chosen display name. Implements flexible identity requirement, separate from authentication username, upholds normalization. E.g. "Jane D."
- `bio`: Short biography field. Implements requirements for expressive/optional profile data; null if user left blank. 3NF; not mixed with system identity.
- `avatar_uri`: Avatar image URI - Implements profile customization; URI to profile image if present. Upholds normalization: actual file stored in separate attachment table.
- `website`: Personal website URI. Optional extra info; good for professional profiles. Nulls preserved for privacy. 3NF compliance (not in auth).
- `location`: Optional location for user. Provides for geography-based statistics or voluntary self-disclosure; optional for privacy. 3NF (won’t be used for enforcement or regional rules).

### `discussionboard_member_authentications`

Member authentication methods - Implements secure credentials, multi-method login, and audit requirements. 

Stores hashed passwords, external ID references, last login timestamp, and auth tokens where needed. 3NF: authentication split into own table with FK to member. 

Usage: Support classic email/password, future-proof for SSO/OAuth extensions.

Relationships: Each member can have multiple credentials (for multi-provider login/fallback).
Security: No cleartext passwords; only hashed tokens or references. Unique per (provider, username/email).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: FK to member identity this credential belongs to. References [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `provider`: Authentication provider e.g. 'local', 'google', 'kakao'. Implements requirement for flexible login. Used in uniqueness check.
- `provider_identifier`: Provider-unique identity (e.g. email for local, user ID for external). Implements multi-method login and support for identification challenges.
- `password_hash`: Hash of password or auth token (never cleartext). Null for OAuth-type logins (where external token not stored after exchange). Enforces security by avoiding password in main member table. 3NF compliance.
- `last_login_at`: Last successful login datetime for credential. Implements auditing per security NFR.

### `discussionboard_member_suspensions`

Records member suspensions for rules enforcement (Moderation/Business Rules).

Represents suspending/blocking users temporarily or permanently. Tracks when, why, and by whom suspension was issued or revoked. 3NF—suspension details not mixed with member core or moderator/action logs.

Usage: Determine posting eligibility, fulfill 2-year audit retention (business rule). Suspension info drives API/feature gating.

Relationships: FK to member. Optionally records moderator/admin who issued/ended action.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: FK to affected member. Indicates who is/was suspended. References [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `issued_by_moderator_id`: FK to moderator who issued suspension (if from moderator). References [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators). Null if action was admin only.
- `issued_by_admin_id`: FK to admin who issued suspension (if admin). References [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins). Null if not admin action.
- `reason`: Suspension reason/notes. Implements business rule for tracking justification and fulfills audit requirement. E.g. 'Repeated off-topic posts'.
- `starts_at`: Suspension start date/time. Implements gating logic (when member loses privileges). Upholds normalization (event data outside status field).
- `ends_at`: Suspension end date/time (null if permanent/active). 3NF (not derived, always recorded as explicit field).
- `revoked_at`: When (if ever) suspension was revoked/cancelled before scheduled end. Null if not revoked or full term served.

### `discussionboard_moderator_actions`

Moderator action logs for audit and transparency (Moderation & Business Rules). 

Stores immutable records of moderator intervention: edit, delete, warning, suspension, tag approval, etc. Implements requirements for transparency, reporting, and appeal/audit workflows. 

Strictly 3NF - action log is separated, not mixed with member core. Includes full details for future analytics and review.

Key relationships: FK to moderator who acted, affects other entities by reference. Used directly in admin dashboard, and for providing appeal evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_moderator_id`: FK to moderator who performed the action (must exist in moderator table). References [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators).
- `action_type`: Type of action performed (e.g. 'edit_post', 'delete_comment', 'issue_warning', 'suspend_member', 'approve_tag'). Implements business rule for clear log granularity and enables filtered reports. No calculation—just event type storage.
- `target_type`: Type of entity affected (e.g. 'post', 'comment', 'member', 'tag'). Needed for correct log analysis and future extensibility.
- `target_id`: ID of target entity—may reference various tables depending on action_type/target_type. Implements need to audit what exact record was affected by an action. (No FK since polymorphic.)
- `details`: Full description of action details, justification, or notes. Helps implement transparency & fulfill legal/audit/compliance requirements.
- `action_at`: Timestamp of when the action was taken. For reporting and workflow tracking.

### `discussionboard_boards`

Board definition entity - Implements section 2.3 Content Operations and 4. Business Rules, supporting organization of discussions by topic (e.g., 'Politics', 'Economics'). 

Business explanation: This table holds the definitions of all boards visible in the system, each representing a broad topical area. Fully normalized: each board is atomic with no denormalized or pre-calculated data. Example: 'Global Politics', 'Macroeconomics'.

Key relationships: May be referenced by board topics; may reference categories (from other components) for further organization. 
Special behaviors: Board codes must be unique.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the board entity.
- `discussionboard_category_id`: Parent category's [discussionboard_categories.id](#discussionboard_categories). Organizes boards under broader discussion categories (category is managed by another domain).
- `code`: Board code - Implements unique identification for boards for routing and business logic. Example: 'POLITICS', 'ECONOMICS'. Ensures normalization; not derived from name. Usage: programmatic API references.
- `name`: Board name - Implements display and search requirements. Used for UI listing. Normalized atomic field.
- `description`: Board description - Implements business rule for onboarding and help text. Provides context to users. Example: 'Discuss current events and policy in global politics.'
- `is_active`: Whether the board is currently active and visible to users. Supports moderation/administrative workflows. Implements part of business rule for board visibility.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of board creation. Required for audit and governance. Used in onboarding and reporting. Not pre-calculated. Always present.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for the board. Enables tracking of administrative changes. Part of audit trail compliance.

### `discussionboard_board_topics`

Topics within each board - Implements section 2.3 Content Operations (thread creation) and logical separation of user-created conversations under boards.

Business explanation: Each topic is a user-defined thread for discussion within a specific board, such as 'Presidential Elections 2025'. Topics refer to boards and have atomic fields for normalization. Fully normalized; per-topic data only, no denormalized aggregates.

Key relationships: References discussionboard_boards as parent; referenced by threads (in another schema); references topic tags for categorization.
Special behaviors: Topic codes are unique per board; topics are never global.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the board topic entity.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Parent board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards). Organizes this topic within a board. Required association for business logic and enforcement of domain boundaries.
- `code`: Topic code, unique per board - Implements unique identification for user-facing links or moderation. Example: 'ELECTIONS', 'Q4_OUTLOOK'.
- `title`: Topic title - Implements user requirement for conversation subjects. Example: '2025 Presidential Elections Discussion'. Normalized atomic field.
- `description`: Descriptive summary of the topic for onboarding/search. Example: 'A space to debate strategies, candidates, and international impact.'
- `created_by_member_id`: Creator's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Reference to the member who created the topic. Implements functional requirement for traceability and audit.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp. Used for ordering and audit trails, required by audit and reporting requirements.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for the topic, for audit trail and modification control.

### `discussionboard_topic_tags`

Topic tag definitions - Implements requirement for curated, moderated topical tagging of discussions (see business rules section 4 and functional requirement 2.4).

Business explanation: Stores curated list of tags that can be assigned to topics, supporting search and categorization. Fully normalized - tags are atomic and not denormalized. Proposed tags managed elsewhere; this table is only for approved/curated tags.

Key relationships: Referenced by board topics or threads for categorization. 
Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint on tag name; tags are not auto-accepted and require moderator/admin approval via separate processes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the topic tag entity.
- `name`: Tag name (unique) - Implements business rule for curated tags. Example: 'Elections', 'Policy', 'Economics'. Searchable and atomic for normalization.
- `is_active`: Whether tag is enabled for assignment to topics or threads. Implements moderation requirement for hidden/disabled tags.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of tag creation - supports audit and governance. Always present.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp, supporting change tracking for moderation/audit.

### `discussionboard_board_announcements`

Moderator/admin announcement entity - Implements requirement 2.6 (Notifications & Communication), enabling information dissemination within boards.

Business explanation: Contains announcements or system messages linked to specific boards (e.g., rule updates, special events). Announcements are always linked to a board, have a title/body, and track who published them. Fully normalized, no denormalized aggregates. 

Key relationships: References discussionboard_boards, admin/moderator (publisher) via foreign keys. Referenced by notification logic in other components for in-app/email alerts.
Special behaviors: Soft deletion supported via deleted_at. Announcements must be orderable by creation timestamp.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the announcement.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Target board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards). All announcements are scoped to a specific board. Implements section 2.6 Notification flows.
- `published_by_admin_id`: Admin/moderator's [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins) who published the announcement. Used for audit and permission control.
- `title`: Announcement title - Implements requirement for concise notification. Example: 'Rule Change: Civility Policy Updated'.
- `body`: Full message body - Implements detailed notification requirement. Markdown supported. Example: 'The board's civility policy has changed...'.
- `is_pinned`: If true, announcement is 'sticky' on board; implements business rule for highlighting key messages. Only one active pin per board at a time (enforced in API logic).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp; enables ordering and audit trace.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp for tracking changes and audit.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp; if not null, announcement is hidden but not physically deleted (supports audit/legal retention).

### `discussionboard_threads`

Discussion Thread entity - This implements the foundational requirement for organizing topic-based discussions (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, 2.3, 2.4). 

Represents a top-level topic or conversation within a board, containing metadata about the origin, categorization, and lifecycle of the thread. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating threads from posts/comments and referencing users and boards via foreign keys only. For example, a thread initiates a new discussion about a political or economic topic, to which users may contribute posts and comments.

Key relationships: Relates to boards (discussionboard_boards) and users (discussionboard_members) via foreign keys, and is referenced by posts. 
Special behaviors: Only thread creators or moderators/admins may edit/delete; status may be updated by system or moderation actions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each thread.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Belonged board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards). Thread is attached to a specific board or category.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Creator's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Indicates which member started this thread.
- `title`: Thread title - Implements requirement for descriptive, searchable topics. Must be unique within the board to prevent confusion. E.g., "Political Reform 2025: National Dialogue". Ensures normalization by storing only atomic string data.
- `description`: Thread description/body - Implements the need for detailed context. Business meaning: Introductory explanation; markdown supported. Ensures normalization by having one plain text field per thread.
- `status`: Thread status - Implements business process control (e.g., 'open', 'closed', 'locked'). Used by moderators/admins to control discussion activity.
- `created_at`: Thread creation timestamp. Required for audit and ordering. 3NF compliance by storing time info only in this field.
- `updated_at`: Thread update timestamp, maintained on edits. 3NF compliant.
- `deleted_at`: Thread deletion/soft-delete timestamp. Nullable - only set if thread is deleted, keeps the data for retention/audit trail.

### `discussionboard_posts`

Discussion Post entity - Implements the core requirement for contributions within threads (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, 2.3). Business purpose: Individual user posts, representing the main argument/content, within a given thread.

Each post is linked to a parent thread and the creating member, without duplicating thread or user information, thus maintaining strict normalization. E.g., a user expresses their view or arguments on a thread topic via a post.

Key relationships: Links to discussionboard_threads (the topic context) and discussionboard_members (the writer). Referenced by discussionboard_comments. 
Special behaviors: Can be edited/deleted by author or moderation subject to business rules.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each post.
- `discussionboard_thread_id`: Parent thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads). Defines which thread the post belongs to.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Author member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Who wrote this post.
- `body`: Main post content/body. Supports markdown for formatting. 3NF: Only pure text; no embedded member or thread info.
- `created_at`: Post creation time, for ordering and audit trail.
- `updated_at`: Last update time, maintained on edits.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp. If null, post is visible; if set, post is deleted but retained for audit/legal purposes.

### `discussionboard_comments`

Discussion Comment entity - Implements the requirement for threaded discussion under posts (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, 2.3, 2.4). Business purpose: Enables replies to posts to enable in-depth discourse. 

Each comment references its parent post and (optionally) a parent comment (for nested replies). Maintains 3NF by referencing posts/members and storing only one level of content per field. For example, a user responds to a post or another user's argument.

Key relationships: Belongs to a post, created by a member. May link to a parent comment via foreign key (used for threading).
Special behaviors: Deletion is by setting deleted_at; edits update updated_at.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Parent post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). Indicates which post the comment belongs to.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Comment author's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Who wrote the comment.
- `parent_id`: Parent comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments). Enables threaded/nested replies. Nullable: only set for replies, not top-level comments.
- `body`: Comment text/content. Business meaning: User's reply or discussion contribution. Normalized by storing only the text.
- `created_at`: Comment creation time. Used for ordering, audit, and display.
- `updated_at`: Comment last update timestamp. Updated on edits for audit trail.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp. Preserves audit trail on deletion. Null if comment is still live.

### `discussionboard_comment_replies`

Discussion Comment Reply entity (shallow reply index) - Implements explicit requirement for efficiently tracking direct comment replies (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, discussion flows and threaded conversations).

This table maintains a normalized, junction-like mapping between comments and their direct replies. Useful for fast queries and enforcing reply relationships without embedding reply structure in-line. For example, every reply to a comment generates a row here, which can be traversed for building reply trees.

Key relationships: Both fields are foreign keys to discussionboard_comments. No duplication of content, ensuring 3NF.
Special behaviors: Deletion is handled via the referenced comment's own deletion marker.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment-reply relationship.
- `comment_id`: The parent comment [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments).
- `reply_id`: The direct reply comment [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments).
- `created_at`: Reply relationship creation time. For audit trail and fast reply tree building.

### `discussionboard_post_attachments`

Discussion Post Attachment entity - Implements the need for posts to include attached files (04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, 2.3). Maintains normalized separation between a post and its files.

For example, a PDF, image, or spreadsheet attached to a discussion post. This keeps document/file metadata atomic and notifies the upload pipeline.

Key relationships: Linked to a discussionboard_post, and references file storage/URI.
Special behaviors: Deletions remove only the attachment, not the post.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each attachment.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Parent post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). The post this attachment belongs to.
- `file_uri`: Attachment file URI/location. Stores where the file is retrievable (S3, static hosting, etc.). Ensures normalization by keeping only the pointer, not embedded file.
- `file_name`: Display name of the attachment file. For user readability and identification; atomic text field per file.
- `file_type`: Attachment file MIME type (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'). Used to display/hide/preview accordingly. Business meaning: file type constraints and display logic.
- `uploaded_at`: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded. Enables audit/control flow.
- `uploaded_by`: Uploader's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Member that uploaded the file. Not a foreign key but value is a UUID.

### `discussionboard_post_likes`

Stores each instance of a member liking a post. Implements Interaction requirement 2.1, which enables users to upvote/like posts for engagement and reputation calculations. Ensures full normalization (3NF) as this table only contains atomic data about the actor and the action, with all relationships explicit and no calculations or denormalization. Used whenever a member clicks 'like' on a post; supports trending features and user feedback mechanisms. Key relationships: references posts and members (already existing); unique on (post, member) to prevent duplicate likes; deletion cascades if the post or member is removed. Special: soft deletion not required, as unliking deletes the row.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each like entry.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Target post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). Links the like to a specific post.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Liking member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Identifies who liked the post.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the like was recorded. For audit logging and activity timelines. Implements reporting/audit requirements.

### `discussionboard_post_dislikes`

Stores each instance of a member disliking a post. Implements Interaction requirement 2.1 and 2.4, supporting user expression and automating moderation signals. Fully normalized (3NF) – atomic event of a dislike, with member and post identity, no calculations. Used when a member clicks 'dislike' on a post; feeds into moderation workflows. Key relationships: references to posts and members (already existing). Unique on (post, member) – one dislike per member per post. Special: row deleted if member cancels dislike.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each dislike entry.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Target post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). Connects dislike to post.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Disliking member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the dislike was made. Supports activity logs and reporting. Requirement: audit trail.

### `discussionboard_comment_likes`

Tracks member likes for each comment. Implements Engagement requirements (2.1) for feedback on comment quality and interaction patterns. 3NF enforced: only references comment and actor, with no non-key dependencies. Example: Used to highlight 'popular' comments or calculate feedback scores. Key relationships: references comments and members. Each member may like a comment once (unique composite key). Deleting a comment/member removes likes. No denormalization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment like.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: Target comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments). Connects like to comment.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who liked this comment.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this comment like was added. Required for activity logs and analysis.

### `discussionboard_comment_dislikes`

Tracks member dislikes for each comment. Implements Engagement and Community Health requirements, enabling members to indicate problematic comments and feeding into moderation if thresholds surpassed. 3NF assured: each record is atomic and relates solely to a discrete user action and its object. Example: Used in triggering auto-flagging of comments. Uniqueness constraint prevents multiple dislikes by same member per comment. Connected to comments and members; row deleted if action undone.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment dislike.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: Target comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments). Connects dislike to comment.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Disliking member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `created_at`: Timestamp of comment dislike event. Supports moderation and audit logs.

### `discussionboard_post_reports`

Tracks when a member reports a post as inappropriate/spam. Implements functional and business rules (see sections 2.5, 4 in requirements), providing critical audit, moderation, and abuse detection. Fully normalized structure; all aggregates handled in reporting. Used to initiate moderation against a post, with links to member, post, and reason. Example: member flags a post for hate speech. Uniqueness constraint: one report per member per post. Key relationships: posts and members. Soft/hard deletes as per moderation outcome.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique for each report instance.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Flagged post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Reporting member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `reason`: Human-readable reason for report (profanity, spam, etc.). Ensures normalization (atomic string data), no categorization here (handled elsewhere).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the report is made. Required for reporting flow and moderation traceability.

### `discussionboard_comment_reports`

Tracks each time a member reports a comment as abusive/inappropriate. Implements moderation trigger requirements (sections 2.5, 4), audit logging, and rate-limiting enforcement. Strictly normalized (3NF), atomic event reference. Key relationships: attached to comment and member, no non-key attributes. One report per member per comment (unique composite key). Used for rate-limiting and moderation response automation. Example: 'report' on an offensive comment.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment report.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: Reported comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments).
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Reporting member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `reason`: Reason for reporting the comment. Worksheets atomic requirement (normalized text, not categorical/aggregated).
- `created_at`: Timestamp of report event; required for traceability (enterprise and legal purposes).

### `discussionboard_tag_proposals`

Tracks proposals for new topic tags, per business rule 4. Members propose tags awaiting moderator/admin review; supports platform curation, anti-abuse, and community-driven structure. Complies with 3NF: atomic proposal event, linked to actor (member), no state duplication. Example: member submits new tag 'economic-inequality'. Moderator resolves outside this table. One unique proposal per member/content/tag combo enforced. Relationships: member (who proposed), tag (proposed string), created_at. Special behaviors: tag field is plain string (proposed, not yet accepted).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each tag proposal.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who proposed new tag.
- `proposed_tag`: Proposed topic tag string. Enforces normalization (atomic text), not categorized (categorization is result of moderation).
- `created_at`: Timestamp of tag proposal. Used for workflow, audit, and process automation.

### `discussionboard_reports`

Report entity - Implements the 'Moderation Reporting' requirement in the requirements analysis. This table tracks all member-initiated reports against posts/comments, ensuring normalized audit trails. For example, it records when a member reports a comment for abuse. Key relationships: reported_by_member_id and resolved_by_moderator_id both reference actors in the system. Special behaviors: maintains clear normalization, no denormalized status/actions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each report.
- `reported_by_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who reported the content.
- `resolved_by_moderator_id`: Moderator's [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators) who resolved this report (nullable if not resolved or auto-resolved).
- `target_post_id`: ID of reported post; only set if reporting a post. For normalization: one of post or comment must be filled, never both.
- `target_comment_id`: ID of reported comment; only set if reporting a comment. For normalization: at least one of post or comment must be filled, never both.
- `reason`: Reason or message explaining the report. Atomic value to ensure normalization. For example, 'Spam' or 'Offensive language'.
- `status`: Workflow status (e.g. 'pending', 'reviewed', 'actioned', 'dismissed'), enabling state-based moderator/automation tracking. Atomic string for normalization.
- `created_at`: When the report was created. Required for audit.
- `resolved_at`: When the report was resolved. Null if unresolved.

### `discussionboard_moderation_logs`

Moderation audit log - Implements the audit trail logging requirement, recording every moderator/admin action. Maintains normalized references to users, posts, comments, and detailed action descriptions. For example, logs when a moderator deletes a post. Key relationships: references moderator and affected entity (post/member/comment). Immutable records for compliance and user trust.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies a moderation log event.
- `moderator_id`: Moderator's [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators) who performed the logged moderation action.
- `target_member_id`: ID of affected member, if action was user-targeted. Nullable for content-only actions.
- `target_post_id`: ID of affected post, if any. Null otherwise. Follows 3NF.
- `target_comment_id`: ID of affected comment, if any. Null otherwise. Follows 3NF.
- `action_type`: Normalized code describing the moderation action (e.g. 'deleted_post', 'suspended_user'). Required for consistent audit analysis.
- `action_details`: Freeform message for context/explanation of action. Maintains normalization by storing details, not computed fields.
- `created_at`: When the moderation action took place. Required for time-based audits.

### `discussionboard_suspension_records`

Suspension record - Implements the 'User Suspension' business rule, recording member suspensions (who, when, duration, revoked, etc) for audit and policy enforcement. Each record ties to the member, issuing moderator, and optionally, the revocation event. Clear normalization and referential integrity is enforced. Used by backend to enforce site restrictions on suspended users.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Identifies each suspension event.
- `suspended_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who is suspended.
- `issued_by_moderator_id`: Moderator/admin's [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators) issuing the suspension.
- `start_at`: Start time of suspension. Not nullable. For audit and enforcement logic.
- `end_at`: End time; null if permanent.
- `reason`: Moderator's reason for suspension, atomic string field. For example, 'Multiple code of conduct violations'.
- `revoked`: True if the suspension has been formally revoked/freed before end_at. Supports workflow around appeal and moderation audit.
- `created_at`: When the record was created.
- `revoked_at`: If revoked, when the suspension was ended early. Nullable.

### `discussionboard_warning_records`

Warning record - Table for warnings issued to members. Implements 'Warnings and Escalations' from business rules. Tracks member, issuer, timestamp and detailed warning message. 3NF maintained: atomic fields, referenced users. Provides historical audit for escalation (multiple warnings before suspension) in normalization-compliant structure.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Identifies each warning issued.
- `warned_member_id`: Warned member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `issued_by_moderator_id`: Moderator's [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators) who gave the warning.
- `reason`: Flexible string reason or warning details. For example, '1st warning for inappropriate language.'
- `created_at`: Timestamp of warning action.

### `discussionboard_content_flags`

Content flag - Records system or moderator flags on threads/posts/comments for filtering, abuse detection or moderation queues. Implements 'Automated & Manual Flagging' requirement in requirements analysis. Fully normalized; foreign keys for user/content sources, atomic flag attributes. Used to queue content for moderator review or for auto-hide. Key relationships: references flagged post/comment and flag setter (by member or moderator).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for each flagged content event.
- `flagged_post_id`: Flagged post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). Nullable if flag set on comment only.
- `flagged_comment_id`: Flagged comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments). Nullable if flag set for post only.
- `flagged_by_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) if the flag was set manually. Nullable for automated/system flags.
- `set_by_moderator_id`: Moderator's [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators) if the flag was set by a moderator. Nullable for automated/user flags.
- `flag_type`: Atomic string code (e.g. 'spam', 'profanity', 'abuse') indicating flag reason.
- `flagged_at`: Timestamp when flag was applied. Used for queue/audit compliance.
- `auto_flagged`: True if the flag was set by system/automation (not a user or moderator). Maintains workflow clarity.

### `discussionboard_notifications`

Discussion Board Notification - Implements the notification delivery and logging requirement as detailed in the Requirements and Business Rules document. This model stores every notification event, such as a reply, mention, moderation update, or announcement, ensuring both reliable delivery and audit trail. Business purpose: accurately targets member accounts and tracks delivery/read states. Maintains strict 3NF normalization; each notification event is atomic, referring to exactly one recipient. Usage examples: generating member notification lists, marking messages as read, auditing notification delivery timelines. Key relationships: references discussionboard_members. Special behaviors: notification records are immutable and individually timestamped for delivery and read receipts.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the notification record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Recipient member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). References the user who receives this notification. Maintains referential integrity and supports targeted delivery.
- `type`: Notification type, e.g. 'reply', 'mention', 'moderation', 'announcement'. Ensures atomic, categorical classification and supports filtering. Example: 'comment_reply', 'moderator_notice'.
- `title`: Notification title/subject. Briefly summarizes the event. Example: 'You've received a new comment reply.'
- `body`: Main content of the notification. Full textual message (e.g., 'Alice replied to your comment ...'). Normalized so that each field is atomic.
- `url`: URL to take the user directly to the relevant thread/post/moderation record. Atomic, optional field only present if the notification involves a direct link.
- `delivered_at`: Timestamp when the notification was delivered. Must be filled at the time of sending for traceability.
- `read_at`: Timestamp indicating when the user read the notification. Nullable if unread.
- `created_at`: When notification record was created. Used for robust audit trails and business intelligence.

### `discussionboard_member_notification_settings`

Discussion Board Member Notification Settings - Implements members' personalized notification delivery settings as described in user journeys and requirements. Each record holds a member's per-channel and per-type notification preferences, supporting full normalization and a single row per user. Ensures no redundant or derived data. Typical use: allows members to mute certain notification types/channels while leaving others active. Key relationships: unique 1:1 with discussionboard_members. Special behaviors: one record per member; nullable only for updated_at if not yet updated. Used for programmatically querying or modifying user preferences.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the settings record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Foreign key to the user's account. Enforces 1:1 mapping for user preference storage.
- `in_app_enabled`: Whether in-app notifications are enabled for this member. Used for quick delivery flag checks. Example: true for active, false for muted in-app alerts.
- `email_enabled`: Whether email notifications are enabled for this member. Ensures atomic tracking and filtering by delivery channel.
- `reply_notification_enabled`: Whether to alert for replies to the member's content. Each flag is atomic, representing a unique notification scenario.
- `mention_notification_enabled`: Whether to alert when the member is @mentioned. Stored atomically and normalized from other notification preferences.
- `moderation_notification_enabled`: Whether moderation alerts (actions, warnings, suspensions) are enabled for this user. Supports opt-out privacy/business use cases.
- `announcement_notification_enabled`: Whether board-wide announcements should be pushed to this user. Complies with business requirement for member-driven preference control.
- `created_at`: When this preference record was created. For compliance and audit trail integrity.
- `updated_at`: When this preference record was last updated. Accurate for reviewing user setting changes over time.

This API endpoint performs the logical deletion of a single post within a discussion thread. Upon receiving a valid authenticated DELETE request for a specific post ID, the system checks:

1. User permissions/role: Only the original post owner, moderator, or admin may initiate the delete.
2. Post state: Ensures post is not already deleted or part of an ongoing moderation action (e.g., being reviewed).
3. Consistency with business rules: Sets deleted_at with the current timestamp, records the action in the audit log, and triggers notifications if required.

If the user is authorized and the post exists, the API updates the post's deleted_at, returning a success response. If permissions are lacking or the post does not exist, returns relevant error. Soft deletion ensures the post is hidden from views but kept for legal/audit compliance. This endpoint is closely related to endpoints for post retrieval, creation, editing, reporting, as well as moderation audit endpoints.

discussionboard_members DB 테이블의 검색/조회/감사 비즈니스 로직 파라미터와 매핑됩니다.
각 필드는 optional입니다.

IPageDiscussionboardMembers.description:
Paginated list of board member records.

This type provides a page of members along with pagination metadata, such as current page and total count, used for directory, admin overview, and advanced filtering. Aligns with standard IPage<T> container types.

id.description:
Unique member identifier. References the main user entity in the Discussion Board system (see discussionboard_members in Prisma schema).

Used as foreign key in profiles, authentications, posts, and moderation actions.

joined_at.description:
Member join date/time in ISO 8601 format. Indicates when the registration was successfully completed.

Aligns with audit and history requirements of the system.

status.description:
Current account status, e.g., 'active', 'pending', or 'suspended'. Business rules govern which APIs/features are available per status.

Reflects member enablement and privilege flows.

IDiscussionboardMembers.description:
Discussion Board member (user) entity type.

Captures the minimal identity fields for a system user and provides primary linkage for posts, authentications, and profile. Reflects core account state as defined in the discussionboard_members table.

joined_at.description:
The registration join date/time (ISO 8601). Must be provided by the API at registration time.

Required to fulfill audit/logging functions.

status.description:
Initial member status, typically 'active' or 'pending'.

Access rights and onboarding flow may depend on this value.

IDiscussionboardMembers.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for member registration.

Specifies the minimal properties needed when a new user is created in the system (see business rules for registration and onboarding).

status.description:
Member status field update. Allows for status transitions (e.g., 'suspended', 'active').

Typical use cases include admin- or system-triggered state changes. This is optional to allow partial updates.

IDiscussionboardMembers.IUpdate.description:
Member update payload.

Currently, only the status field is supported for direct update via this schema. Expansion possible in future versions.

member_id.description:
Optional: Filter moderator role assignments by specific member ID.

When provided, narrows search/query for moderators linked to a given member.

promoted_from.description:
Optional: Filter only moderator assignments promoted after this timestamp (ISO8601).

Used for administrative search tools and audit analytics.

promoted_to.description:
Optional: Only retrieve moderator assignments promoted before this timestamp (ISO8601).

Helps support range searches in dashboards and history views.

is_active.description: Optional: Filter for currently active moderator assignments (demoted_at is null).

DiscussionBoardModerators.IRequest.description:
Moderator list/search request schema.

Allows advanced filtering, paging, and search for moderator assignments via admin UI or API.

DiscussionBoardModerators.IPage.description:
Paginated result of moderator role assignments, including relevant metadata for navigation, sorting, and display.

Used for admin role management UIs and dashboards.

id.description: Unique moderator assignment record ID.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member's unique identifier (foreign key to members table).

oneOf.description: If present, date/time moderator was demoted (null if currently active).

demoted_at.description: If present, date/time moderator was demoted (null if currently active).

DiscussionBoardModerators.description:
Moderator role entity, includes reference to member, promotion/demotion state, and audit trail.

Matches the structure of discussionboard_moderators table in the Actors domain.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member's ID to promote to moderator. Must refer to an existing, eligible member account. Business rules prevent duplicate or concurrent roles per member.

promoted_at.description: Datetime when moderator role is assigned.

DiscussionBoardModerators.ICreate.description:
Request to create a moderator assignment by promoting a member.

Admin-initiated role elevation to moderator status.

demoted_at.description: If provided, marks this moderator role assignment as ended at the specified time. Supports soft demotion flows and privilege audits. Optional.

DiscussionBoardModerators.IUpdate.description:
Moderator role assignment update.

Used for demotion or privilege state changes tracked via this role entity.

member_id.description: Optional: Filter for admin role assignments belonging to a specific member. Used in broader role audits and assignment histories. Allows precise admin role lookup or targeted revocation workflows.

elevated_from.description: Optional: Restrict search to admins elevated after this date/time (ISO8601). Workflow for role review, escalation, and analytics.

elevated_to.description: Optional: Restrict detection to admins elevated before this date/time (ISO8601). Enables time-span-based analytics or review screens.

DiscussionBoardAdmins.IRequest.description:
Admin assignment search/list request object.

Designed for advanced access, audit, or reporting flows in role management features.

DiscussionBoardAdmins.IPage.description:
Paginated array of admin assignment records with metadata for navigation and analytics.

Standard admin list page wrapper.

id.description: Unique record identifier for admin role assignment. Uniquely identifies an admin role for a member.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member account UUID linked to admin role. Foreign key to core actors table.

elevated_at.description: Datetime when admin privileges were granted. Used for audit, role traceability, and privilege management.

DiscussionBoardAdmins.description:
Admin role assignment entity schema. Refers to a member, elevation timestamp, and unique assignment ID.

Enables management and audit of high-level role states.

discussionboard_member_id.description: ID of the member to be promoted to admin. References a unique user in the Actors domain. Value must match an existing, active member's UUID. Required for establishing the admin relationship.

elevated_at.description: Timestamp for when admin privileges were granted to the member. This is a required, server-generated or client-provided ISO 8601 datetime indicating role elevation, supporting audit compliance as per business rules.

DiscussionBoardAdmins.ICreate.description: Object used to create a new admin assignment in the system. Based on discussionboard_admins Prisma table and relevant to role elevation operations. Aligns with business requirement for explicit privilege tracking and audit compliance.

elevated_at.description: The new timestamp for admin privilege assignment, if being changed. Must be ISO 8601 datetime. Used for correcting elevated role records or forced role recertification by system administrator.

DiscussionBoardAdmins.IUpdate.description: Object for updating the admin elevation record for a member in the admin system. Syncs with business audit and privilege recertification requirements for role management.

display_name.description: Display name string for filtering member profiles. Enables admin/moderator user search for a visible or preferred nickname. Optional, case-insensitive partial matches allowed.

joined_after.description: Find members who joined after this ISO 8601 datetime. Supports onboarding reports and retention queries.

joined_before.description: Find members who joined before this ISO 8601 datetime. Allows for time range user profile audits or stale account filtering.

page.description: Pagination: the page number (1-based).

limit.description: Pagination: maximum number of items to return per page.

IDiscussionboardThreads.IRequest.description: Payload for listing and searching discussion threads. Fulfills business/domain requirements for scalable, filterable thread retrieval—used in admin, mod, and member UI in the discussion board system.

IPageIDiscussionboardThreads.description:
A paginated list of thread records for the DiscussionBoard system.

This schema is used as a standard response for list APIs returning discussion threads, providing both an array of thread records and pagination metadata. The 'pagination' object describes page number, limits, total records, and total pages, while 'data' holds the thread entities. Reflects use cases for APIs that need to fetch multiple threads in a scalable fashion, supporting UI thread lists and administrative moderation workflows.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each thread. See discussionboard_threads.id

discussionboard_board_id.description: Foreign key to Board (discussionboard_boards.id). Indicates which board this thread belongs to.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Foreign key to Member (discussionboard_members.id). The member who created this thread.

title.description: Thread title. See discussionboard_threads.title. Must be unique per board and descriptive for subject/content discovery. Supports advanced search UI.

oneOf.description: Optional thread description/body. See discussionboard_threads.description. Supports markdown for in-depth context at thread initiation. Nullable if no description.
Optional thread description/body. See discussionboard_threads.description. Supports markdown for in-depth context at thread initiation. Nullable if no description.

description.description: Optional thread description/body. See discussionboard_threads.description. Supports markdown for in-depth context at thread initiation. Nullable if no description.

status.description: Thread status (e.g. 'open', 'closed', 'locked'). See discussionboard_threads.status. Determines whether users can participate or view.

created_at.description: Thread creation timestamp (ISO 8601). Fulfills ordering/audit/log requirements. See discussionboard_threads.created_at.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp. Tracks edit history; reflects most recent change. See discussionboard_threads.updated_at.

oneOf.description: Soft-delete timestamp. If set, thread is considered deleted but retained for audit/data retention. See discussionboard_threads.deleted_at.
Soft-delete timestamp. If set, thread is considered deleted but retained for audit/data retention. See discussionboard_threads.deleted_at.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp. If set, thread is considered deleted but retained for audit/data retention. See discussionboard_threads.deleted_at.

IDiscussionboardThreads.description:
Discussion thread entity for the DiscussionBoard platform, as defined in discussionboard_threads schema.

Represents a top-level topic within a board. Contains all atomic fields for UI, audit, and API management. The entity separates UI-visible data (title/description/status) from relational identifiers (board/member), with required timestamps for audit compliance.

discussionboard_board_id.description: Target board ID to which this thread will belong. Required.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Creator member ID. Required.

title.description: Thread title (must be unique within the board). Required.

oneOf.description: Optional thread description/body supporting markdown.
Optional thread description/body supporting markdown.

created_at.description: Timestamp of thread creation (ISO 8601 format).

IDiscussionboardThreads.ICreate.description:
Schema for creating a new thread entity on the DiscussionBoard.

Follows the requirements of discussionboard_threads for registration of a topic—including links to board and member, title, (optional) description, initial status, and creation timestamp. Used as request body for thread creation endpoint.

title.description: New or updated thread title. If changed, must comply with board-uniqueness constraint.

oneOf.description: New thread description/body (markdown supported). Nullable.
New thread description/body (markdown supported). Nullable.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update (ISO 8601). Should correspond to edit action.

IDiscussionboardThreads.IUpdate.description:
Schema for updating an existing thread entity on the DiscussionBoard.

Permits updating the thread title, description/body, and status. 'updated_at' is required for audit and edit tracking. All properties are optional except updated_at, so only fields to be changed need be included.

discussionboard_thread_id.description: (Optional) Filter: posts belonging to specific thread ID.

discussionboard_member_id.description: (Optional) Filter: posts created by member.

created_at_from.description: (Optional) Filter: posts created after this date/time (ISO 8601).

created_at_to.description: (Optional) Filter: posts created before this date/time (ISO 8601).

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts from 1). Optional.

limit.description: Maximum number of posts per page. Optional.

sort.description: Sort order: e.g. 'created_at desc', 'created_at asc', 'updated_at desc'. Optional.

IDiscussionboardPosts.IRequest.description:
Request schema for searching/listing DiscussionBoard posts with filtering, pagination, and sorting.

Used as request body for post-listing endpoint, enables advanced queries for feeds, dashboards, and administration.

IPageIDiscussionboardPosts.description:
A paged response with list of DiscussionBoard posts for feeds or moderation views.

Provides required 'pagination' structure and data array as per IPage contracts, holding DiscussionBoard post entities for API responses.

id.description: Primary key (ID) for the post. See discussionboard_posts.id.

discussionboard_thread_id.description: Foreign key to thread. Which thread this post belongs to. See discussionboard_posts.discussionboard_thread_id.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Foreign key to member. Author of the post.

body.description: Main post content/body (markdown supported). Business field required for thread participation.

created_at.description: Post creation datetime (ISO 8601). For audit trails and ordering.

oneOf.description: Soft-delete timestamp (nullable). If set, post is logically deleted in UI/API results.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp (nullable). If set, post is logically deleted in UI/API results.

IDiscussionboardPosts.description:
DiscussionBoard post entity. Defines all fields for core thread/post structures, links to thread/member, and auditing timestamps.

Used for direct display in APIs, UI, and audit/compliance reports. Conforms to discussionboard_posts table. 'body' is required and always markdown-capable.

discussionboard_thread_id.description: Thread ID to which this post is to be attached. Required.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member ID for the post author (required).

created_at.description: Timestamp of post creation.

IDiscussionboardPosts.ICreate.description:
Request body schema to create a new post in a discussion thread.

Represents all required input fields per DB and business logic: links to thread/member, content, and audit field for timestamp. Used in frontend post creation UI and backend APIs.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of post update (ISO 8601, required for audit).

IDiscussionboardPosts.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema to update an existing discussion post.

Allows updating only the body/content and timestamp. Use for member edits and moderation. No other mutable fields.

id.description: Primary key for the post. See discussionboard_posts.id

discussionboard_thread_id.description: Thread ID this post belongs to.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member who authored the post.

created_at.description: When the post was created.

deleted_at.description: If set, the post is deleted/hidden in the UI. Null otherwise.

IDiscussionboardPost.description:
DiscussionBoard post resource entity object. Used as response payload for post queries, including fetch by id and delete (soft-delete) return types.

Fields match discussionboard_posts DB entity: UUIDs for relations, markdown body, and standard audit timestamps (creation/update/deletion).

discussionboard_member_id.description: (Optional) Filter by member/author id.

parent_id.description: (Optional) Filter for comments that are replies to a specific comment (threaded discussion).

created_at_from.description: (Optional) Only comments created after this datetime.

created_at_to.description: (Optional) Only comments created before this datetime.

page.description: Results page number for pagination (optional).

limit.description: Maximum number of comments per page (optional).

sort.description: Sort criteria, e.g. 'created_at desc', 'created_at asc', 'updated_at desc' (optional).

IDiscussionboardComment.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for searching/listing comments (discussionboard_comments) with filters, search, and pagination.

Enables advanced queries for threaded forum display, admin review, and hierarchical UI.

IPageIDiscussionboardComment.description:
Paged response of DiscussionBoard comments, with thread/post context for each and pagination metadata for UI and backoffice moderation workflows.

Returns an array of comment entities for forum/audit/reporting views.

id.description:
Primary key and unique identifier for the comment. Corresponds to the discussionboard_comments.id field in the database. Used to reference the comment in all thread and moderation flows.

This must be a valid UUID. It is required and used for all GET/UPDATE/DELETE operations.

discussionboard_post_id.description:
The parent post's unique identifier the comment belongs to. Corresponds to discussionboard_posts.id. Required for relation mapping and data retrieval in APIs, feeds, and moderation.

Valid UUID, must reference an existing post.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
Unique ID of the user who authored the comment. Corresponds to discussionboard_members.id. Used in author attributions, auditing, moderation workflows, and permissions enforcement.

Must always be a valid user referencing a member.

oneOf.description:
If this comment is a reply to another comment, this stores the parent comment's ID (discussionboard_comments.id). Supports threading/hierarchy. Null for top-level comments.

body.description:
Actual text/content of the comment. Markdown formatting supported according to business rules. Content is subject to moderation, length, and formatting checks per requirements.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was created (ISO 8601, e.g., '2025-07-22T11:00:00+09:00'). Included for display, audit, and sorting purposes.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the comment. Used for edit history, audit, and UI freshness logic. Always present.

oneOf.description: If set, indicates this comment was soft-deleted at this datetime. Used for moderation, compliance, and to support legal/audit retention. If null, the comment is live.

deleted_at.description: If set, indicates this comment was soft-deleted at this datetime. Used for moderation, compliance, and to support legal/audit retention. If null, the comment is live.

IDiscussionboardComment.description:
Full comment entity as stored in the forum DB. Implements business requirements for nested/threaded discussion, moderation, audit, and compliance as described in the requirements analysis and Prisma schema. Includes all atomic and relational attributes required for user interface, audit trails, and legal compliance. Each comment can reference a parent for reply trees, supports markdown, and is subject to moderation.

Read-only or computed fields (like counts/reactions) are not included; see related endpoints for those.

Covers all CRUD and moderation flows, enforces API consistency and traceability.

discussionboard_post_id.description: The ID of the parent post this comment is attached to. Must reference an existing post. This is a required relation for threading and reply trees.

discussionboard_member_id.description: ID of the member who is making the comment. Must reference a valid, non-suspended user in the system.

body.description: Comment text content. Markdown supported if permitted by forum configuration. Must not be empty; subject to length and formatting constraints.

oneOf.description: If this is a reply to another comment, specify the parent comment's UUID (nullable for top-level comments). Must refer to a valid comment inside the same post/thread.
If this is a reply to another comment, specify the parent comment's UUID (nullable for top-level comments). Must refer to a valid comment inside the same post/thread.

parent_id.description: If this is a reply to another comment, specify the parent comment's UUID (nullable for top-level comments). Must refer to a valid comment inside the same post/thread.

Shape for API calls to create a new comment within a thread's post. Matches core business requirements for user discussion flows, hierarchical threading, and content auditability.

All fields must match business rules as specified in entity design, and relations are checked in backend logic.

body.description: The new or updated comment text/body. Required. Must pass moderation and validation. May be rejected if under edit lock, moderation hold, or compliance block.

Only owners or privileged users may update; enforcement is handled at API layer/permissions.

data.description: Array of comment reply relationships for the current page.

IPageIDiscussionboardCommentReply.description: Paginated results for comment reply relationship search. Used in moderation, dashboard, or discussion views aggregating reply structure. Follows standard IPage<T> pattern.

created_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601). When the reply relationship was created. Used for ordering, dashboard replay, audit, and query filtering.

IDiscussionboardCommentReply.description: Mapping record for parent-reply comment relationships in threaded discussion. Satisfies reply tree retrieval, UI rendering, audit trail, and moderation navigation workflows. Maintains full normalization (no embedded comment content here).

reply_id.description: ID of the reply (child) comment (discussionboard_comments.id). Must reference a different, existing comment in the same thread/post.
