IDiscussionboardPostAttachment.IRequest.description: Query structure for searching and paginating post attachments. Used in user uploads UI, moderator panels, and attachment overviews.

data.description: Array of post attachment records for current page.

IPageIDiscussionboardPostAttachment.description: Output structure for paginated attachment queries. Follows standard IPage<T> format for indexed lists.

id.description: Unique identifier for post attachment (discussionboard_post_attachments.id). Required for reference and audit.

discussionboard_post_id.description: The post's unique identifier to which the attachment belongs. Required for all attachment management actions.

file_uri.description: URI or storage pointer to the uploaded file (e.g., S3, CDN, file service). Must be a safe URL or storage reference per security rules. Used for serving and downloading files.

file_name.description: Filename displayed to users for this attachment. Must be a valid, safe string (no path traversal, XSS, etc.). Enforced by backend validation and upload.

file_type.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'). Used for validation and preview logic.

uploaded_at.description: Datetime file was uploaded (ISO 8601 format). Important for audit, sorting, and business rules.

uploaded_by.description: ID of the user who uploaded the attachment. Tracks responsible member, enforces upload/edit/delete permissions.

IDiscussionboardPostAttachment.description: Complete record for a file attached to a post. Satisfies business, security, and audit requirements for file metadata. Used in attachment display, download, and moderation APIs.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Target post's unique identifier; associates file to this post. Must exist and be write-accessible to the uploader.

file_uri.description: Storage location or CDN URI for the actual uploaded file. Must conform to backend security and file validation rules.

file_name.description: Display filename for the attachment, used in UI/file pickers and for downloads.

file_type.description: MIME type string, e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'. Enforced by backend during upload for virus/malware/content policy.

uploaded_by.description: ID of the member uploading the file. Used to validate ownership, auditing, and permission enforcement.

IDiscussionboardPostAttachment.ICreate.description: Structure for new file attachment uploads in post content. Used in submission, moderation, and initial display workflows.

file_name.description:
The display name of the attachment file. A user-friendly name presented in the UI; atomic text value used for identification and download purposes.

Maps to the 'file_name' column in Prisma's 'discussionboard_post_attachments' table. If updated, changes how the file appears attached to the post—not used for the file storage name.

file_type.description:
MIME type representing the file, e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'.

This field dictates preview/handling logic on the frontend. Maps to 'file_type' in the Prisma schema; updating may impact interface and download. Set to the new type when the file is replaced.

file_uri.description:
The URI or location of the actual file. Used to retrieve/download the file.

Mirrors the 'file_uri' field in the database. An update here may point to a new file version or replacement file. Must be a valid URI/URL (can be a remote or internal resource, such as AWS S3, CDN, etc.).

IDiscussionboardPostAttachment.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for post attachment record in the Discussion Board system. Each field corresponds to metadata for a file attached to a forum post. When updating, all three fields must be supplied to fully replace the attachment metadata. Descriptions based on the 'discussionboard_post_attachments' Prisma model and platform requirements.

This object is used in PUT/UPDATE operations and provides strong normalization between request data and audit tracking for compliance.

status.description:
Status message of the delete operation. Indicates whether the deletion was successful or provides error context.

Typical values could be 'success', 'not found', 'already deleted', or detailed error messages, depending on business logic.

oneOf.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the resource was deleted.

Null if the object was previously deleted or the resource did not exist. Used for audit, compliance, and confirming time of logical/soft delete. Mirrors 'deleted_at' fields in Prisma soft-delete patterns.

ISO 8601 timestamp when the resource was deleted.

Null if the object was previously deleted or the resource did not exist. Used for audit, compliance, and confirming time of logical/soft delete. Mirrors 'deleted_at' fields in Prisma soft-delete patterns.

deleted_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the resource was deleted.

Null if the object was previously deleted or the resource did not exist. Used for audit, compliance, and confirming time of logical/soft delete. Mirrors 'deleted_at' fields in Prisma soft-delete patterns.

IDeleteResult.description: Result object returned after a DELETE (or soft-delete) API operation. Provides status of the delete action along with a timestamp if the action succeeded and was recorded. Standardized for Discussion Board resource deletion results.

discussionboard_post_id.description:
Filter by target post's UUID. Only like records associated with this post will be returned.

Directly aligns with 'discussionboard_post_id' in 'discussionboard_post_likes'. Allows clients to query for all likes on a single post.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
Filter by the member's UUID who gave likes. Can be used for dashboards showing what a particular member has liked.

Directly aligns with 'discussionboard_member_id' in 'discussionboard_post_likes'.

from_created_at.description: Start of the time range for filtering like records, using ISO 8601 datetime. Only likes created at or after this are returned.

to_created_at.description: End of the time range for like records, using ISO 8601 datetime. Only likes created at or before this timestamp will be included.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1 if not provided. Used for navigating large result sets.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page. Defaults to system standard if not set. Used for pagination control.

IDiscussionboardPostLike.IRequest.description: Request object for listing or searching DiscussionBoard post like records. All fields are optional and provide filtering/pagination for querying the 'discussionboard_post_likes' table. Maps to engagement analytics and personal dashboard needs.

data.description: List of post like record objects matching the list query.

IPageIDiscussionboardPostLike.description: A paginated list of 'discussionboard_post_likes' records. Combines pagination meta (page/limit/total/etc.) and the core data set for client consumption. Used across all API endpoints returning bulk like data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the post like record. Directly matches 'id' in the Prisma schema table. Used for referencing and auditing.

discussionboard_post_id.description:
Post UUID that this like is attached to. Connects the like event with the forum post.

References 'discussionboard_post_id' in 'discussionboard_post_likes'.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member UUID for the user who liked the post. Shows who performed the like action.

created_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601) when the like was given. Used in analytics and UI feeds.

IDiscussionboardPostLike.description: Represents a single member's like on a discussion post in the 'discussionboard_post_likes' table. Every like is atomic, immutable, and tied to both a member and a post per business rules. This model is central for engagement, trending calculations, and moderator review.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Target post's UUID. When creating a like, this is the post to be liked. Must refer to a valid post already in the system.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member UUID who is liking the post. Normally derived from authentication context.

IDiscussionboardPostLike.ICreate.description: Payload for creating a new post like record in the Discussion Board. Requires both the post and acting member IDs. Fulfills business logic: only one like per post/member pair; API must check for duplicates.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Target post's UUID for updating a like record. Normally cannot be changed for existing records, but included for update compliance if schema allows post reattribution.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member UUID for updating like attribution (typically not allowed in production, but present for audit/admin fix use cases).

IDiscussionboardPostLike.IUpdate.description:
Update data for a post like record in the Discussion Board. These fields may be only exposed to admins/moderators for audit correction. In production, like relationships are normally immutable post-creation.

Mirrors 'discussionboard_post_likes' schema fields.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Filter for dislikes on a given post. UUID aligns with 'discussionboard_post_id' in the table.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Filter for dislikes from a specific member. UUID aligns with 'discussionboard_member_id' in 'discussionboard_post_dislikes'.

from_created_at.description: Low-end of creation time filter, using ISO 8601 datetime. Inclusive.

page.description: Page number for pagination.

limit.description: Limit of records per page.

IDiscussionboardPostDislike.IRequest.description: Query/filter object for searching dislikes on posts within the Discussion Board. All fields are optional and provide flexible querying for moderation tools, analytics, or user dashboards.

data.description: Array of post dislike records for the current result page.

IPageIDiscussionboardPostDislike.description: Paginated result set for post dislikes. Combines pagination metadata and result array of dislike entries. Used by moderator dashboards, analytics, and user profile/history screens.

id.description: Unique identifier for the post dislike record. Corresponds to 'id' in 'discussionboard_post_dislikes'.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Target post's ID. Indicates which post the dislike is for.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member's UUID who disliked the post.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the dislike event occurred.

IDiscussionboardPostDislike.description: Represents a single member's dislike on a discussion post. Stored atomically in 'discussionboard_post_dislikes'. Each record is an immutable event reflecting negative feedback, used for moderation and analytic workflows.

discussionboard_post_id.description: UUID of the post being disliked. Must exist in the system.

discussionboard_member_id.description: UUID of the member disliking the post. Set from the authentication/user context.

IDiscussionboardPostDislike.ICreate.description: Payload for creating a post dislike record in the Discussion Board. Requires post and member UUID. Validates no duplicate entries are created for post/member pair per business rule.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Target post for updating a dislike record. In practice, should only be used in admin/audit scenarios for post reattribution.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Updated member UUID for the dislike event, if necessary for audit correction.

IDiscussionboardPostDislike.IUpdate.description:
Update object for post dislike record on the Discussion Board. These operations are generally highly restricted and intended only for audit/admin repair workflows; normal like/dislike relationships should not be changed in end-user flows.

Properties match the table schema; all fields optional for partial updates.

comment_id.description:
The unique identifier of the comment for which likes are being queried.

Referenced from the discussionboard_comments table. Used in filtering which comment's like records to retrieve.

Based on the business rule, only likes for valid (non-deleted) comments will be returned.

member_id.description:
The unique identifier of the member whose likes are being queried.

References the discussionboard_members table. Used to filter comment likes by the member who performed the action.

If omitted, lists likes from all members subject to permissions.

created_after.description:
Optional filter to retrieve likes created after a specified ISO 8601 timestamp.

Useful for time-based queries in moderation and analytics workflows.

If not supplied, no lower time bound is applied.

created_before.description:
Optional filter to retrieve likes created before a specific ISO 8601 timestamp.

Supports time-windowed searches for reporting or analytics.

If not specified, no upper bound filter is applied.

page.description: Pagination: the number of the page to retrieve (1-based). Default is 1.

limit.description: Pagination: maximum number of comment like records per page. Default is 20, maximum is 100.

oneOf.description: Sort key for ordering comment likes. Supported values: 'created_at', 'comment_id', 'member_id'. Default is 'created_at'.
Sort key for ordering comment likes. Supported values: 'created_at', 'comment_id', 'member_id'. Default is 'created_at'.
Sort key for ordering comment likes. Supported values: 'created_at', 'comment_id', 'member_id'. Default is 'created_at'.

sort_key.description: Sort key for ordering comment likes. Supported values: 'created_at', 'comment_id', 'member_id'. Default is 'created_at'.

oneOf.description: Sort order for the selected key. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Default is 'desc'.
Sort order for the selected key. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Default is 'desc'.

sort_order.description: Sort order for the selected key. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Default is 'desc'.

IDiscussionboardCommentLike.IRequest.description:
Request object for searching, filtering, and paginating comment like records in the DiscussionBoard.

Maps to fields in the discussionboard_comment_likes table. Used by moderators, admins, and members to list engagement records with applied filters and sorting.

Each property corresponds to an atomic query parameter, strictly normalized as per database and business rule definitions.

data.description: A list of comment like objects returned in this page.

IPageIDiscussionboardCommentLike.description:
Paginated list/summary container for discussionboard_comment_likes records.

Contains both the results array and pagination metadata, with references to the schema that enforces normalized/atomic data in each list entry.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the comment like record.

References the primary key in the discussionboard_comment_likes table.

Enables precise, atomic tracking for audit trail, analytics, and reporting workflows.

discussionboard_comment_id.description:
The unique identifier of the comment that received the like.

Foreign key to discussionboard_comments.id. Directly supports engagement analytics, abuse-reporting correlations, and UI summaries of who liked each comment.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
Unique identifier of the member who performed the like.

References discussionboard_members.id. Critical for audit, rate-limiting, and eligibility checks in business rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this like was recorded by the system.

Stored as an ISO 8601 string. Used for time-bounded queries, user history, and engagement trend analyses.

IDiscussionboardCommentLike.description:
Represents one like action performed by a member on a comment in the DiscussionBoard.

Atomic record in the discussionboard_comment_likes table. All properties map to database fields and are required for audit, analytics, and engagement logic.

discussionboard_comment_id.description:
The unique identifier of the comment to like.

Must reference a valid, non-deleted comment in discussionboard_comments.

This field is required for the like creation business logic.

IDiscussionboardCommentLike.ICreate.description:
Schema for creating (adding) a like to a comment in the DiscussionBoard system.

Used in POST endpoints.

Requires specifying the comment to like. The liking member is inferred from the authentication context.

Ensures clean normalization and enforcement against duplicate likes by the same member for the same comment.

discussionboard_comment_id.description:
(If supported) Change the comment being liked. Usually restricted; changing the reference after creation is rare but permitted in audit/admin correction scenarios.

References discussionboard_comments.id.

Should not allow setting to a comment already liked by the same member.

IDiscussionboardCommentLike.IUpdate.description:
Schema for updating a comment like record, usually in moderation or audit correction scenarios.

In standard operations, likes are immutable. However, admins or business logic may allow limited updates (e.g., correcting the referenced comment).

All updates must be audit-logged with before/after state.

comment_id.description:
Filter by the unique identifier of the comment whose dislikes are being queried.

References discussionboard_comments.id.

Used in dislike engagement analytics and moderation.

member_id.description:
Filter by the member who performed the dislike.

References discussionboard_members.id.

Supports per-user dislike tracking for feature and audit use cases.

created_after.description:
Retrieve dislikes created after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

Useful for time-series analytics, reporting, and burst analysis in content moderation.

created_before.description:
Retrieve dislikes created before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

Used for data-windowing and snapshot reporting.

page.description: Pagination: page number to retrieve (1-based). Default is 1.

limit.description: Pagination: maximum records per page. Default is 20, max is 100.

oneOf.description: Sort key: one of 'created_at', 'comment_id', 'member_id'. Default: 'created_at'.
Sort key: one of 'created_at', 'comment_id', 'member_id'. Default: 'created_at'.
Sort key: one of 'created_at', 'comment_id', 'member_id'. Default: 'created_at'.
Sort order: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Default: 'desc'.
Sort order: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Default: 'desc'.

IDiscussionboardCommentDislike.IRequest.description:
Request object for searching/filtering/paginating comment dislike records, following the atomic structure of discussionboard_comment_dislikes.

Each field is atomic and filterable; designed for analytics, moderation, and user history queries.

Follows normalized, audit-friendly DB column mapping.

data.description: Array of comment dislike records present in this paginated result.

IPageIDiscussionboardCommentDislike.description:
Paginated page container for comment dislikes (engagement/analytic/feedback purposes).

Includes result data and page cursor metadata. Atomic and compliant with standard IPage pattern.

id.description: The unique identifier for the comment dislike event/record. Atomic and references primary key in discussionboard_comment_dislikes.

discussionboard_comment_id.description:
Comment ID indicating which comment was disliked.

Foreign key from discussionboard_comments.id.

Required for both audit and UI engagement analytics.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
The member ID who performed the dislike.

References discussionboard_members.id. Supports audit, anti-abuse, and feedback systems.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) when the dislike event was recorded by the system.

Supports analytics, moderation, and time-limited engagement queries.

IDiscussionboardCommentDislike.description:
Atomic record representing a single dislike event for a comment in the DiscussionBoard.

Rows follow strict normalization; all fields are required for audit and analytics.

Reflects engagement/feedback for threaded comments.

discussionboard_comment_id.description:
UUID of the comment to be disliked.

Must belong to a valid, non-deleted comment.

Business logic prevents duplicate dislikes by the same member for the same comment.

This is required for creating the dislike record.

IDiscussionboardCommentDislike.ICreate.description:
Schema for creating a dislike event for a comment, attached to the active member from the authentication context.

Enforces normalization: each entry is an atomic dislike event for a specific member and comment.

Handles duplicate and permission checks as per business logic.

discussionboard_comment_id.description:
(If business rules allow) Update the referenced comment for this dislike record. Normally, dislikes are immutable but admin/audit flows might permit correction or re-attribution.

References discussionboard_comments.id.

IDiscussionboardCommentDislike.IUpdate.description:
Schema for updating a comment dislike record—usually for audit/admin error correction.

Regular member operations don't permit modification, but admins may update for compliance.

Every change must be audit-logged.

post_id.description:
Restrict search to reports for a specific post. References discussionboard_posts.id.

Critical for moderation workflow filtering and targeted abuse review.

reporting_member_id.description:
Limit results to reports filed by this member. References discussionboard_members.id.

Used for member history review, rate-limiting enforcement, and abuse prevention.

created_after.description:
Retrieve post reports created after this date/time (ISO 8601).

Enables time-windowed analysis for analytics and reporting dashboards.

created_before.description:
Retrieve post reports created before this date/time (ISO 8601).

Helps provide time-bounded results for reporting and audit trails.

reason_search.description:
Full-text search within the report reason field.

Used for advanced filter scenarios where specific types of reports (spam, abuse) are targeted for review.

page.description: Pagination: which page of results to return (1-based, default 1).

limit.description: Pagination: maximum records per page (default 20, maximum 100).

oneOf.description: Sort key field. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'post_id', 'reporting_member_id'. Default is 'created_at'.
Sort key field. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'post_id', 'reporting_member_id'. Default is 'created_at'.
Sort key field. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'post_id', 'reporting_member_id'. Default is 'created_at'.

sort_key.description: Sort key field. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'post_id', 'reporting_member_id'. Default is 'created_at'.

oneOf.description: Sort order: 'asc' or 'desc'. Default is 'desc'.
Sort order: 'asc' or 'desc'. Default is 'desc'.

IDiscussionboardPostReport.IRequest.description:
Search and filter object for querying reported posts for moderation workflows.

All fields are mapped to a strict, normalized database schema in discussionboard_post_reports.

Used by moderation UIs to efficiently filter, search, and review reported post events per business rules.

data.description: The list of DiscussionBoard post report records for this page.

IPageDiscussionboardPostReport.description:
Page container type for a paginated result of post abuse/spam report records in the DiscussionBoard.

Follows the IPage<T> pattern for page metadata and result data arrays.

id.description:
The unique identifier for this post report. It corresponds to the 'id' field in the Prisma table `discussionboard_post_reports`. This value is required for consistent referencing and system operations.

UUID values ensure global uniqueness and support system-wide identification, including audit and moderation workflows.

discussionboard_post_id.description:
The identifier of the post being reported. References a record in the posts entity, not a foreign key constraint, but used to trace moderation and reporting chains.

Supports audit, abuse tracking, and is used in moderation dashboards.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
Identifier of the member who reported the post. This is a foreign key to the reporting user, essential for quota enforcement (e.g., max 10 reports/day) and audit compliance.

Used for tracking user engagement, abuse control, and reporting rate limits.

reason.description:
The reason provided by the member for reporting this post. Supports normalized atomic reasons. Examples include 'Spam', 'Hate speech', etc.

Freeform string per business rule. Used for moderation filtering and insight analytics.

created_at.description:
The timestamp the report was created. Full ISO8601 string. Used for rate-limiting and workflow ordering.

Required by business compliance and for effective moderation review.

IDiscussionboardPostReport.description:
A record of a post report submitted by a member, stored in the Prisma table `discussionboard_post_reports`. Represents an abuse/reporting event linked to a particular post for moderation review.

Includes all key fields required for audit, business rule, and review workflows in the discussion board system.

discussionboard_post_id.description: UUID identifier of the post the member is reporting. Cross-references `discussionboard_posts.id`.

reason.description: Human-readable reason for reporting this post. Examples: 'Spam', 'Offensive language'. Fulfills normalized business logic.

IDiscussionboardPostReport.ICreate.description:
Input payload used to create a new post report in the discussion board system. Sent by authenticated users when submitting a report via the API.

Matches the writable fields as per the Prisma schema and business rules. `discussionboard_member_id` (the reporter) is inferred from authentication context.

reason.description: (Optional) Updates the reason provided for this report. May be used for correction or moderator commentary, as permitted by business rules.

IDiscussionboardPostReport.IUpdate.description:
Payload used for updating an existing post report record. Primarily used by moderators or admins for workflow correction.

Includes only mutable fields. In most cases, only `reason` can be revised.

success.description: Indicates whether the delete operation was successful.

deleted_id.description: UUID of the deleted report, confirming which entity was removed. For audit and client UI confirmation.

IDiscussionboardPostReport.IDeleteResult.description: Result/confirmation object returned by a delete operation on a post report in the system. Used for client confirmation and audit trail.

discussionboard_comment_id.description: Filter for reports related to a specific comment. UUID as per the `discussionboard_comments.id` field.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Filter to show reports made by a specific member (the reporter). Corresponds to `discussionboard_members.id`.

reason.description: Text search or filter for the report reason. Matches normalized 'reason' field for analytics or workflow triage.

page.description: Pagination: page number. Used to browse paginated results. Follows the system's standard page-based navigation.

limit.description: Pagination: maximum records per page. Used for API scalability and frontend client batching.

IDiscussionboardCommentReport.IRequest.description:
Query and filter parameters for listing/searching comment reports in the moderation view. Used to retrieve paginated results by moderators/admins.

All parameters are optional, supporting flexible query composition for moderation dashboards.

data.description: Array of comment report summary/details.

IPageDiscussionboardCommentReport.description:
Paginated list result structure for comment reports. Matches the standard IPage<T> interface for the discussion board system.

Supplies both page metadata and array of comment report objects, supporting robust UI/data traversal for moderators/admins.

id.description: The unique identifier for this comment report. Refers to the `id` in the Prisma `discussionboard_comment_reports` table.

discussionboard_comment_id.description: The comment that was reported. Corresponds to `discussionboard_comments.id`.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member (reporter) who filed the report. Corresponds to `discussionboard_members.id`.

reason.description: Reason string describing why the report was made. Freeform by business rule.

created_at.description: The timestamp when the report was submitted, ISO8601.

IDiscussionboardCommentReport.description: Entity representing a report submitted against a comment by a member. Matches an entry in the `discussionboard_comment_reports` Prisma table, including all key audit, relationship, and business logic fields required for moderation workflow.

reason.description: Freeform reason from the reporting member, e.g., 'Spam', 'Profanity', etc. Used for moderation workflow.

IDiscussionboardCommentReport.ICreate.description: Input object for creating a new report against a comment. Fields align with writable data by end-users in the API, and mapped to the discussion board's moderation reporting workflow.

reason.description: Revised/updated reason for report, allowed under moderation audit/correction or special business rules.

IDiscussionboardCommentReport.IUpdate.description: Payload for updating (correcting) the reason or details for an existing comment report. Only used by moderation/admin workflows as allowed by business policy.

success.description: Indicates if the deletion was successful.

deleted_id.description: UUID of the deleted comment report.

IDiscussionboardCommentReport.IDeleteRes.description: Result/confirmation object returned after deleting a comment report. Used for client workflow and audit confirmation.

discussionboard_member_id.description: (Optional) Filter proposals by member ID. Useful for showing a member's submissions for moderation review.

proposed_tag.description: (Optional) Partial or exact-match filter on the tag string proposed by members. Used for search and moderation curation.

page.description: Pagination page number for listing moderation requests.

limit.description: Max number of proposals to return per page. Used for pagination, scalability, and rate-limiting.

IDiscussionboardTagProposal.IRequest.description: Filter and query parameters for listing/searching tag proposals submitted by members. Used in the moderation and curation dashboard APIs. All properties are optional for flexible queries.

data.description: The array of tag proposal summary/detail objects for the page.

IPageDiscussionboardTagProposal.description: Paginated array result structure for listing tag proposals. Follows system-standard IPage<T> response contracts to handle metadata and records.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for each tag proposal.

This is the atomic ID for referencing the tag proposal record in all moderation, admin workflow, and business logic layers. It is stored as a UUID and ensures 3NF normalization by not duplicating or calculating information elsewhere. Used in querying, audit logs, and reviewing proposals.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
Member's unique identifier (UUID) who is proposing the tag to the forum.

Links directly to the member (user) object. Fulfills business and audit requirements for tracing who proposed each tag and supporting accountability. Never nullable.

proposed_tag.description:
String value of the tag being proposed. Must be unique for each member proposal.

Carries the atomic tag label string that the proposing user entered. Used in tag creation flows, moderation, and anti-abuse logic. Supports uniqueness constraints, profanity filtering, and business validation at the API/business layer.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp for when the tag proposal was submitted.

Supports audit/lifecycle flows for the tag curation system, rate-limiting logic for proposals, and analytics. Always present.

IDiscussionboardTagProposal.description:
Discussion Board Tag Proposal entity representing an atomic proposal for a new topic tag to be added to the curated set.

Refer to the requirements regarding curated tags and proposal/approval moderation flow. This model is normalized and tracks proposals per member for audit, curation, and abuse prevention. Every tag proposal is linked to its proposing member, supports rate-limiting and anti-abuse business logic, and enables end-to-end lifecycle tracking for tag onboarding.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
UUID of the member proposing the tag, fulfilling the business requirement to associate all proposals with an authenticated user.

Key for validation, curation review, and auditing.

proposed_tag.description:
String representing the tag being proposed for addition.

Ensures 3NF compliance. Uniqueness required (per member) and subject to moderation, profanity filtering, and system-wide tag policy. Examples: 'Elections', 'Macroeconomics', 'CampaignFinance'.

IDiscussionboardTagProposal.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new tag proposal.

Provided by a member submitting a new tag for moderator/admin review. Only authenticated, non-suspended members may create proposals. Used in rate-limiting and tag curation flows.

proposed_tag.description: Updated tag string for the proposal. Must comply with tag guidelines, maintain uniqueness per member, and be subject to all business and moderation filtering rules.

IDiscussionboardTagProposal.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing tag proposal.

Permits a member or privileged moderator/admin to change the string of a proposed tag before review. Must comply with tag naming, uniqueness, and community rules.

reported_by_member_id.description:
UUID of the reporting member (who filed the report), for filtering/search.

Aids in moderation review, audit, and rate-limiting reporting flows.

resolved_by_moderator_id.description: UUID of the moderator who resolved this report (if resolved). Useful for filtering by handler or admin in moderation dashboards.

status.description:
Moderation workflow status for filtering (e.g. 'pending', 'reviewed', 'actioned', 'dismissed').

Enforces search, queueing, and reporting flows per requirements.

target_post_id.description: UUID of target post, for searching reports by content. Supports reporting, audit, and moderation use-cases.

target_comment_id.description: UUID of the target comment for filtering comment-specific reports.

created_from.description: Lower-bound datetime for filtering reports created after this moment in time.

created_to.description: Upper-bound datetime for filtering reports created before this time.

page.description: Pagination: requested page number (1-based default).

limit.description: Pagination: number of reports per page (API and UI enforce reasonable per-request caps for system health).

IDiscussionboardReport.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for listing or searching moderation reports.

Enables paginated, filterable queries for all moderation reports. Supports queueing, batch review, and audit/reporting use-cases. Reference to business requirements for rate-limiting, workflow status, and moderation dashboard UX.

data.description: Array of report entities for the current result page.

IPageDiscussionboardReport.description:
Paginated search/list result for moderation reports (discussionboard_reports).

Contains queueable result items for moderation dashboards, analytics, and batch admin workflows. Used for implementation of audit trails and review logs.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for each report entity.

Atomic UUID for referencing the report in all moderation, audit, and dashboard logic. Supports audit, appeals, and rate-limiting enforcement.

reported_by_member_id.description: UUID of the member who filed the report. Links to user account history, supports abuse/rate-limiting controls, and allows for statistical dashboards tracking reporting activity.

resolved_by_moderator_id.description: UUID of the moderator who resolved this report. Nullable if unresolved or resolution is automated. Business logic references audit, review, and transparency rules.

target_post_id.description: UUID of the reported post if this report targets a post. Null if not a post report.

target_comment_id.description: UUID of the reported comment if this report targets a comment entity. Null if not applicable.

reason.description:
Human-readable string reason for report (e.g., 'Spam', 'Hate Speech', or custom message).

Refer to content guidelines and moderation policy for required handling, audit, and evidentiary trace.

status.description:
Current workflow status (e.g., 'pending', 'reviewed', 'actioned', 'dismissed').

Enables queueing, automated handling, state transitions, and process tracking for the moderation team.

created_at.description: Timestamp for report creation. Supports audit trails, reporting, and appeals workflows.

resolved_at.description: When the report was resolved (null if unresolved/ongoing). For workflow tracking, audit, resolution, and transparency features.

IDiscussionboardReport.description:
Moderation Report entity representing a flagged post or comment as reported by a board member, tracked through resolution workflow.

Tracks detailed moderation, audit, and appeal status for reported posts or comments. Atomic record used in moderation dashboards, appeals, compliance records. All handling of report is governed by transparency, workflow, and logging business rules.

reported_by_member_id.description: UUID of the member filing the report, ensuring auditability and enforcing business validation/rate limit per user.

target_post_id.description: UUID of the post being reported (nullable—must have either post or comment).

target_comment_id.description: UUID of the comment being reported (nullable—must have either post or comment).

reason.description:
The reason for reporting (free-form or policy-guided string).

May be constrained by content policy, with predefined categories and/or custom entries.

IDiscussionboardReport.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new moderation report.

Member-supplied input for flagging content (post or comment) for review. Must satisfy business/logical enforcement for per-user rate-limiting, content validation, and correctness in targeting either post or comment but not both.

resolved_by_moderator_id.description: UUID of the moderator who is resolving this report. Tracked for audit, transparency, and operational metrics.

status.description: Workflow status after resolution (e.g. 'reviewed', 'actioned', 'dismissed'). Enforced by moderation, audit, and analytics.

resolved_at.description: Timestamp marking when the report was resolved. Required for proper audit/compliance.

IDiscussionboardReport.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating (resolving) a moderation report.

Supplies required information for closing, dismissing, or actioning the flagged content, meeting all compliance, audit, and transparency rules.

moderator_id.description:
UUID of the moderator whose actions are being queried/filtering.

Aids in accountability dashboards and audit logs.

action_type.description: Moderation action type filter (e.g. 'delete_post', 'issue_warning', etc). Enables search by type via dashboard, analytics, or audit review mechanisms.

target_type.description: Target entity type string (e.g. 'post', 'comment', 'member', 'tag'). Allows focused action review according to content or user affected.

target_id.description: UUID of the target entity in question (post/comment/member etc). For use in targeted event search flows.

page.description: Pagination: requested result page index (1-based).

limit.description: Pagination: number of logs per page (API and UI enforce per-request upper limits).

IDiscussionboardModerationLog.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for querying/paginating moderation logs.

Allows filtering by moderator, action type, target, and period for investigation, reporting, or analytics.

data.description: Array of moderation log entries for current page.

IPageDiscussionboardModerationLog.description:
Paginated moderation log result schema.

Carries array of log entities and full pagination info as required for audit review, dashboard query, and process analytics.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for the moderation log entry.

Atomic reference for audit, investigation, and appeals workflows.

moderator_id.description: UUID of the moderator who performed this action. Used for accountability, operational metrics, and appeals tracking.

target_member_id.description: UUID of the affected member if a user-targeted action (nullable where content-only actions are involved). Enables compliance, escalation ladders, contextual appeals.

target_post_id.description: UUID of affected post if action is related to a post (null otherwise). Nested targets handled in audit/business logic.

target_comment_id.description: UUID of affected comment if moderation activity is on a comment. Null for non-comment actions.

action_type.description: String code for log action (e.g. 'delete_post', 'suspend_member'). Categorical and used for operational analytics and audit clarity.

action_details.description: Extra information describing the moderation action. Null if not provided. Supports compliance, appeals reference.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the moderation event took place. For investigation/audit timelines.

IDiscussionboardModerationLog.description:
Moderation log entity representing moderator/admin actions for audit, analytics, and compliance recording.

Each event is standalone and atomic for legal, appeals, and governance requirements. References moderator, target entities (user, post, comment), log action and time, with optional additional detail.

moderator_id.description: UUID of the moderator creating the log event. Needed for accountability, auditing, and workflow linkage.

action_type.description:
String code for the type of moderation event performed (e.g., 'delete_post', 'warn_user').

Open string category enabling operational analytics, reporting, and flexibility in business rule extensions.

target_member_id.description: UUID of affected member, for user-directed actions. Null if event is not user-related.

target_post_id.description: UUID of affected post for content moderation events. Null if unrelated.

target_comment_id.description: UUID of affected comment entity. Null if unrelated to comment moderation.

action_details.description: Optional descriptive narrative explaining what was done, justification, or evidence/log trace. Used for appeals and compliance.

IDiscussionboardModerationLog.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a moderator action log entry.

Enforced for all moderator/admin interventions (delete, suspend, warn, tag action, etc) to provide a traceable action trail per organizational, legal, and community governance requirements.

moderator_id.description: The ID of the moderator who performed or is responsible for the moderation action. Used to track accountability and link actions to specific staff. This field should be a valid UUID string referencing the moderator's unique record.

oneOf.description: ID of the member who is the subject of the moderation action, if applicable. Nullable if the action is not directed at a specific user (e.g., targeting a post or comment instead). Always a valid UUID or null.

ID of the member who is the subject of the moderation action, if applicable. Nullable if the action is not directed at a specific user (e.g., targeting a post or comment instead). Always a valid UUID or null.

target_member_id.description: ID of the member who is the subject of the moderation action, if applicable. Nullable if the action is not directed at a specific user (e.g., targeting a post or comment instead). Always a valid UUID or null.

oneOf.description: ID of the affected post, applicable for actions such as 'delete_post', 'edit_post', etc. Nullable if not relevant for this moderation action. Must be a valid UUID string or null.
ID of the affected post, applicable for actions such as 'delete_post', 'edit_post', etc. Nullable if not relevant for this moderation action. Must be a valid UUID string or null.

target_post_id.description: ID of the affected post, applicable for actions such as 'delete_post', 'edit_post', etc. Nullable if not relevant for this moderation action. Must be a valid UUID string or null.

oneOf.description: ID of the affected comment, applicable for actions on comments. Nullable for non-comment actions. Must be a valid UUID or null.
ID of the affected comment, applicable for actions on comments. Nullable for non-comment actions. Must be a valid UUID or null.

target_comment_id.description: ID of the affected comment, applicable for actions on comments. Nullable for non-comment actions. Must be a valid UUID or null.

action_type.description: Normalized code indicating the type of moderation action (e.g., 'deleted_post', 'suspended_user', etc.). Provides a consistent action taxonomy per business, audit, and reporting needs.

oneOf.description: Additional details, context, or moderator notes for the action. Freeform text to elaborate justification or action outcome. Nullable.
Additional details, context, or moderator notes for the action. Freeform text to elaborate justification or action outcome. Nullable.

action_details.description: Additional details, context, or moderator notes for the action. Freeform text to elaborate justification or action outcome. Nullable.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the moderation action occurred, in ISO 8601 format. Used for audit trails, escalation time analysis, and incident reviews.

IDiscussionboardModerationLog.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for the DiscussionBoard moderation log entity, representing changes to a specific moderator action. This schema supports audit trail corrections, additional data enrichment, or resolving historic moderation entries. Referenced Prisma DB table: discussionboard_moderation_logs.

Each moderation action log documents a single intervention or decision by a moderator, with linkage to the affected member/post/comment (if any), action type, details, and time. Updates may be restricted to certain fields for preserving audit chain integrity. Used by admin and compliance tools.

oneOf.description: ID of the member whose suspension records are being searched for. Nullable to include all members. Used for targeted dashboard queries or appeals workflows.
ID of the member whose suspension records are being searched for. Nullable to include all members. Used for targeted dashboard queries or appeals workflows.

suspended_member_id.description: ID of the member whose suspension records are being searched for. Nullable to include all members. Used for targeted dashboard queries or appeals workflows.

oneOf.description: ID of the moderator who issued the suspension, for filtering. Null indicates no filter. Facilitates moderator activity analysis or audit.
ID of the moderator who issued the suspension, for filtering. Null indicates no filter. Facilitates moderator activity analysis or audit.

issued_by_moderator_id.description: ID of the moderator who issued the suspension, for filtering. Null indicates no filter. Facilitates moderator activity analysis or audit.

oneOf.description: Filtering criterion: Include only started after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Nullable if not filtering by start time.
Filtering criterion: Include only started after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Nullable if not filtering by start time.

start_after.description: Filtering criterion: Include only started after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Nullable if not filtering by start time.

oneOf.description: Filtering criterion: Include only ended before this ISO 8601 timestamp. Nullable if not filtering by end time.
Filtering criterion: Include only ended before this ISO 8601 timestamp. Nullable if not filtering by end time.

end_before.description: Filtering criterion: Include only ended before this ISO 8601 timestamp. Nullable if not filtering by end time.

oneOf.description: If true, only revoked suspensions are included; if false, only non-revoked suspensions. If null, include all regardless of revoked status.
If true, only revoked suspensions are included; if false, only non-revoked suspensions. If null, include all regardless of revoked status.

revoked.description: If true, only revoked suspensions are included; if false, only non-revoked suspensions. If null, include all regardless of revoked status.

oneOf.description: The page number for paginated results. Optional/null means default (typically page 1 in standard paging semantics).
The page number for paginated results. Optional/null means default (typically page 1 in standard paging semantics).

page.description: The page number for paginated results. Optional/null means default (typically page 1 in standard paging semantics).

oneOf.description: Maximum records per page. Helps with pagination UI and dashboard performance. Nullable for default.
Maximum records per page. Helps with pagination UI and dashboard performance. Nullable for default.

limit.description: Maximum records per page. Helps with pagination UI and dashboard performance. Nullable for default.

IDiscussionboardSuspensionRecord.IReques.description: Request body structure for querying or filtering suspension records as implemented for the DiscussionBoard platform (discussionboard_suspension_records). Allows filtering by suspended member, issuing moderator, date ranges, revocation status, and includes pagination. Used in moderator/admin dashboards and compliance reporting.

pagination.description: Pagination meta information describing the current set, total count, pages, etc.

data.description: The array of suspension records returned by the paginated query, filtered as per request criteria.

IPageIDiscussionboardSuspensionRecord.description: Container object for a page of DiscussionBoard suspension records, as used by the platform’s listing APIs. Supports collection listing with paging meta per IPage<T> pattern. See DiscussionBoard business rules regarding minimum retention and paging limits.

id.description: The unique identifier of this suspension record (Prisma PK). Used for audit, dereferencing, and updates.

suspended_member_id.description: ID of the member who is/was suspended. References the member’s main record ID. Required for lookup, dashboard display, and audits.

issued_by_moderator_id.description: ID of the moderator who issued the suspension. Business rule: Must reference a valid moderator, even if suspension is later escalated to admin. Enforced by FK in DB.

start_at.description: The date/time the suspension began. Must be in ISO 8601 format. Used for enforcement windows and time-based policy reporting.

oneOf.description: When the suspension ends, or null for permanent suspensions. Used by enforcement logic and appeal workflows.
When the suspension ends, or null for permanent suspensions. Used by enforcement logic and appeal workflows.

end_at.description: When the suspension ends, or null for permanent suspensions. Used by enforcement logic and appeal workflows.

reason.description: Human-readable or rule-based reason describing why the suspension was issued. Required for audit, compliance, and support. Example: 'Multiple policy violations'.

revoked.description: True if this suspension was lifted before expiration. Records appeal or moderator/admin action. Used for escalation decision analytics.

created_at.description: When the suspension record was created in the system. Used for audit/compliance, appeals, and expiration policies.

oneOf.description: When, if ever, this suspension was revoked. Null if suspension was never lifted early. Required for policy compliance and appeals analytics.
When, if ever, this suspension was revoked. Null if suspension was never lifted early. Required for policy compliance and appeals analytics.

revoked_at.description: When, if ever, this suspension was revoked. Null if suspension was never lifted early. Required for policy compliance and appeals analytics.

IDiscussionboardSuspensionRecord.description: Represents a member’s suspension event within the DiscussionBoard platform. Each record captures details such as issuer, reasoning, starting/ending window, revocation, and audit metadata. Based on discussionboard_suspension_records DB table. All records must be retained per compliance and audit policy.

suspended_member_id.description: ID of the member to be suspended. References the unique member record; must be present in discussionboard_members.

issued_by_moderator_id.description: ID of the moderator/admin issuing the suspension. Only moderators or admins can issue suspensions, per RBAC.

start_at.description: Datetime at which the suspension becomes effective. Format must be ISO 8601. Used for enforcement and audit.

oneOf.description: Datetime when suspension ends (null for indefinite/permanent suspensions). Used for appeal and automatic expiry workflows.
Datetime when suspension ends (null for indefinite/permanent suspensions). Used for appeal and automatic expiry workflows.

end_at.description: Datetime when suspension ends (null for indefinite/permanent suspensions). Used for appeal and automatic expiry workflows.

reason.description: Reason for the suspension, provided by the issuer. Must adhere to business process/legal logging requirements (e.g., not empty, not abusive, etc).

IDiscussionboardSuspensionRecord.ICreate.description: Request body for creating a new member suspension in the DiscussionBoard platform. See business rule/enforcement workflows around permitted durations and allowable issuers. Fulfills audit legality and compliance.

oneOf.description: Update to the scheduled end time for the suspension. Null means make it indefinite/permanent. Used for appeal, extension, or adjustment logic.
Update to the scheduled end time for the suspension. Null means make it indefinite/permanent. Used for appeal, extension, or adjustment logic.

end_at.description: Update to the scheduled end time for the suspension. Null means make it indefinite/permanent. Used for appeal, extension, or adjustment logic.

oneOf.description: Optionally update the explanation or reason for the suspension. Nullable—may leave unchanged when not supplied.
Optionally update the explanation or reason for the suspension. Nullable—may leave unchanged when not supplied.

reason.description: Optionally update the explanation or reason for the suspension. Nullable—may leave unchanged when not supplied.

oneOf.description: Update the revoked status to reflect an appeal or administrative reversal. Null means no change.
Update the revoked status to reflect an appeal or administrative reversal. Null means no change.

revoked.description: Update the revoked status to reflect an appeal or administrative reversal. Null means no change.

oneOf.description: Set or update the date/time of revocation for the suspension. Nullable—null when not setting this flag.
Set or update the date/time of revocation for the suspension. Nullable—null when not setting this flag.

revoked_at.description: Set or update the date/time of revocation for the suspension. Nullable—null when not setting this flag.

IDiscussionboardSuspensionRecord.IUpdate.description: Payload for updating properties of an existing DiscussionBoard suspension record. May be used to adjust time windows, modify reason, or change revoked/revoked_at state. Changes must be audit-trailed per business/compliance policy.

oneOf.description: Filters warning records by warned member. UUID or null for all members.
Filters warning records by warned member. UUID or null for all members.

warned_member_id.description: Filters warning records by warned member. UUID or null for all members.

oneOf.description: Filters warnings by issuing moderator ID. UUID or null for all moderators.
Filters warnings by issuing moderator ID. UUID or null for all moderators.

issued_by_moderator_id.description: Filters warnings by issuing moderator ID. UUID or null for all moderators.

oneOf.description: Return only warnings created after this timestamp. Nullable.
Return only warnings created after this timestamp. Nullable.

created_after.description: Return only warnings created after this timestamp. Nullable.

oneOf.description: Return only warnings created before this timestamp. Nullable.
Return only warnings created before this timestamp. Nullable.

created_before.description: Return only warnings created before this timestamp. Nullable.

oneOf.description: Page number of the request in paginated results.
Page number of the request in paginated results.

page.description: Page number of the request in paginated results.

oneOf.description: Number of records per page (page size).
Number of records per page (page size).

limit.description: Number of records per page (page size).

IDiscussionboardWarningRecord.IRequest.description: Request object for filtering, searching, and paginating warning records in the DiscussionBoard system (discussionboard_warning_records). Used in moderator/admin dashboards and reporting.

pagination.description: Information about current chunk of result-set: current page, limit, total records, page count.

data.description: Warning records associated with this page, result of filter/search.

IPageIDiscussionboardWarningRecord.description: Paginated container for DiscussionBoard warning records utilizing IPage pattern. See business rules for minimum retention, page sizes, and audit history.

id.description: Unique identifier of this warning record. Required for audit referencing and updates.

warned_member_id.description: ID of member who received the warning. Always a valid UUID linked to discussionboard_members.

issued_by_moderator_id.description: ID of moderator who issued the warning. UUID, required for audit, compliance, and chain-of-command.

reason.description: Explanation or context for the warning, compliant with moderation rules. Not null or empty.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the warning was issued. Used for audit and history escalation logic.

IDiscussionboardWarningRecord.description: Warning record for a member within the DiscussionBoard community, as per discussionboard_warning_records DB table. Defines all key audit fields: issuer, member, time, and rationale for escalations and reporting.

warned_member_id.description: ID of member to warn (target user). Must exist in main member table. Required.

issued_by_moderator_id.description: ID of moderator issuing the warning. Must exist, required by business policy.

reason.description: Explanation or context for warning action. Must comply with audit, chain-of-command, and appeal procedures.

IDiscussionboardWarningRecord.ICreate.description: Payload/schema for creating a new warning record in the DiscussionBoard system. Used during member moderation, escalation, and compliance workflows.

oneOf.description: Optionally update the warning reason, context, or message. Null for no change.
Optionally update the warning reason, context, or message. Null for no change.

reason.description: Optionally update the warning reason, context, or message. Null for no change.

IDiscussionboardWarningRecord.IUpdate.description: Payload for updating a warning record within the DiscussionBoard system. Only editable field is the reason/context. Change history must be audit-logged.

oneOf.description: Filter for content flags set by a particular member. Null for all.
Filter for content flags set by a particular member. Null for all.

flagged_by_member_id.description: Filter for content flags set by a particular member. Null for all.

Filter for content flags set by specific moderator. Null for any.

set_by_moderator_id.description: Filter for content flags set by specific moderator. Null for any.

flag_type.description: Type(s) of content flag (e.g., 'spam','profanity','abuse'). Null for all types.

oneOf.description: Filter: restrict to auto-flagged items (by system). Null for all.
Filter: restrict to auto-flagged items (by system). Null for all.

auto_flagged.description: Filter: restrict to auto-flagged items (by system). Null for all.

Filter: Only flags on particular post. Null for any/none.

flagged_post_id.description: Filter: Only flags on particular post. Null for any/none.

oneOf.description: Filter: Only flags on particular comment. Null for any/none.
Filter: Only flags on particular comment. Null for any/none.

flagged_comment_id.description: Filter: Only flags on particular comment. Null for any/none.

oneOf.description: ISO 8601 lower bound for flagged_at date (include only flags after this datetime).
ISO 8601 lower bound for flagged_at date (include only flags after this datetime).

flagged_after.description: ISO 8601 lower bound for flagged_at date (include only flags after this datetime).

oneOf.description: ISO 8601 upper bound for flagged_at date (include only flags before this datetime).
ISO 8601 upper bound for flagged_at date (include only flags before this datetime).

flagged_before.description: ISO 8601 upper bound for flagged_at date (include only flags before this datetime).

Current page (for pagination).

page.description: Current page (for pagination).

oneOf.description: Records per page (pagination chunk size).
Records per page (pagination chunk size).

IDiscussionboardContentFlag.IRequest.description: Request payload for filtering and listing content flags in the DiscussionBoard moderation system. Allows moderators/admins to search by actor, target, flag type, automation, and time.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata object as defined by the OpenAPI standard. This provides detailed information about current page, total records, page limits and how the response was paginated. Referenced from standard IPage template.

data.description: Array of DiscussionboardContentFlag records for the current page. Each entry represents a single content flag as normalized in the moderation audit schema.

IPageIDiscussionboardContentFlag.description:
A page object for discussion board content flag moderation records. This type defines the paged list structure for flagged content in the system, supporting robust auditing of moderation actions. Corresponds to the IPage<T> structure with DiscussionboardContentFlag responses as the records. For full context, see flagging business rules in the Prisma schema and requirements analysis.

The purpose of content flag pagination is to allow efficient browsing, actionable dashboards for moderation staff, and compliance reviews for automated and manual flag triggers.

id.description: Primary key for the content flag record. This is a unique identifier for each individual flag instance. Referenced in other records for traceability and auditability.

oneOf.description: If a post was flagged, this property holds the unique identifier of the post. Nullable if the target is a comment. Ensures normalization by not mixing flag contexts.
If a post was flagged, this property holds the unique identifier of the post. Nullable if the target is a comment. Ensures normalization by not mixing flag contexts.

flagged_post_id.description: If a post was flagged, this property holds the unique identifier of the post. Nullable if the target is a comment. Ensures normalization by not mixing flag contexts.

oneOf.description: If a comment was flagged, this property contains the UUID for the comment. Nullable if the flag is for a post. Maintains atomic distinction between posts and comments as required by moderation schema.

If a comment was flagged, this property contains the UUID for the comment. Nullable if the flag is for a post. Maintains atomic distinction between posts and comments as required by moderation schema.

flagged_comment_id.description: If a comment was flagged, this property contains the UUID for the comment. Nullable if the flag is for a post. Maintains atomic distinction between posts and comments as required by moderation schema.

oneOf.description: The member’s unique identifier who flagged the content. Null if flag was created by automated system or directly by moderator.
The member’s unique identifier who flagged the content. Null if flag was created by automated system or directly by moderator.

flagged_by_member_id.description: The member’s unique identifier who flagged the content. Null if flag was created by automated system or directly by moderator.

oneOf.description: The moderator’s unique ID if the flag was set by manual moderation. Null if not manual or by system/member.
The moderator’s unique ID if the flag was set by manual moderation. Null if not manual or by system/member.

set_by_moderator_id.description: The moderator’s unique ID if the flag was set by manual moderation. Null if not manual or by system/member.

flag_type.description: Atomic type code describing why the content was flagged. Typical values: 'spam', 'profanity', 'abuse', 'automation', etc. Enum may be described externally by platform policy or admin configuration.

flagged_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording exactly when the content flag was set. Fulfills audit/compliance requirement for moderation traceability.

auto_flagged.description: Indicates whether this flag was set by automated system (true) or manually by a user or moderator (false). Fulfills reporting and compliance business logic.

IDiscussionboardContentFlag.description:
Represents a single moderation-flag record for discussion board content. Closely models the discussionboard_content_flags table as described in the moderation domain and Prisma schema.

Flags may relate to posts or comments, and may be set by users, moderators, or automated rules for spam/abuse/profanity/etc. Used to power queue-based moderation interfaces and historical/audit views. The design supports strict normalization for compliance and deep analytics.

oneOf.description: If flagging a post, supply the unique identifier (UUID) for the post. Must not be filled if this flag is for a comment. Validated at API boundary according to content type.
If flagging a post, supply the unique identifier (UUID) for the post. Must not be filled if this flag is for a comment. Validated at API boundary according to content type.

flagged_post_id.description: If flagging a post, supply the unique identifier (UUID) for the post. Must not be filled if this flag is for a comment. Validated at API boundary according to content type.

oneOf.description: If flagging a comment, supply its UUID. Null for post-only flags.
If flagging a comment, supply its UUID. Null for post-only flags.

flagged_comment_id.description: If flagging a comment, supply its UUID. Null for post-only flags.

oneOf.description: ID of the member submitting the flag. If the flag is raised by an automated system or a moderator directly, leave null.
ID of the member submitting the flag. If the flag is raised by an automated system or a moderator directly, leave null.

flagged_by_member_id.description: ID of the member submitting the flag. If the flag is raised by an automated system or a moderator directly, leave null.

oneOf.description: ID of the moderator who sets the flag directly. Null for member/automatic/system flags.
ID of the moderator who sets the flag directly. Null for member/automatic/system flags.

set_by_moderator_id.description: ID of the moderator who sets the flag directly. Null for member/automatic/system flags.

flag_type.description: Required business-logic string specifying why content is flagged (spam, abuse, forbidden, etc.). Must follow platform moderation/business policy enumeration.

auto_flagged.description: If true, this flag is being set by an automated rule or system process. If false, set by a human (member or moderator) as allowed by business logic.

IDiscussionboardContentFlag.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new discussion board content flag. This input type matches the moderation business process as described in the requirements and Prisma schema (discussionboard_content_flags create).

Enforces clear separation between post/comment context, actor responsible for flagging, and reason/type. Supports both automated and manual flags. Validation distinguishes between automated, member, and moderator sources as well as content type.

oneOf.description: If needed, update the post reference for this flag (should only be used to correct or re-attribute context in rare moderation workflows).
If needed, update the post reference for this flag (should only be used to correct or re-attribute context in rare moderation workflows).

flagged_post_id.description: If needed, update the post reference for this flag (should only be used to correct or re-attribute context in rare moderation workflows).

oneOf.description: If required, reassign the target to a different comment. Extremely rare and meant for admin-level corrections.
If required, reassign the target to a different comment. Extremely rare and meant for admin-level corrections.

flagged_comment_id.description: If required, reassign the target to a different comment. Extremely rare and meant for admin-level corrections.

oneOf.description: Update the member reference—should only be used if originally recorded incorrectly. See business policy for editing flags.
Update the member reference—should only be used if originally recorded incorrectly. See business policy for editing flags.

flagged_by_member_id.description: Update the member reference—should only be used if originally recorded incorrectly. See business policy for editing flags.

oneOf.description: Update the assigned moderator if original flag was corrected. Only for moderation/admin use.
Update the assigned moderator if original flag was corrected. Only for moderation/admin use.

set_by_moderator_id.description: Update the assigned moderator if original flag was corrected. Only for moderation/admin use.

flag_type.description: Update/moderate the content flag reason (e.g., if misclassified or investigation reveals different flag type). Value must still conform to policy enumeration.

auto_flagged.description: Update whether the flag is marked as automatically set or not. Used in rare audit corrections or appeals.

IDiscussionboardContentFlag.IUpdate.description:
Update schema for a discussion board content flag record. Used by moderation/admin backend systems for correcting misflagged content or adjusting audit trails in rare workflows. All updates must be audit logged.

Modifications typically only allowed to privileged accounts and with business policy restrictions.

id.description: UUID of the deleted flag record.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp (ISO-8601) marking when the flag was (soft-)deleted from the content moderation queue.

success.description: Indicates whether the deletion of the flag was successful.

IDiscussionboardContentFlag.IDeleteRespo.description:
Response/result object for flag deletion endpoints. Returns details about the flag and the status of deletion for reliable audit and compliance monitoring according to moderation rules.

This type documents the evidence trail for recordkeeping, supporting both user feedback and regulatory reporting.

oneOf.description: Page number for paginated notification results. Optional—defaults to first page if not supplied.
Page number for paginated notification results. Optional—defaults to first page if not supplied.

page.description: Page number for paginated notification results. Optional—defaults to first page if not supplied.

oneOf.description: Optional. Number of notifications per page (system default may apply when absent).
Optional. Number of notifications per page (system default may apply when absent).

limit.description: Optional. Number of notifications per page (system default may apply when absent).

Optional filter: type of notification (e.g., 'reply', 'mention', 'moderation', 'announcement'). Allows filtering by event category; see business rules for system notification types.

type.description: Optional filter: type of notification (e.g., 'reply', 'mention', 'moderation', 'announcement'). Allows filtering by event category; see business rules for system notification types.

Optional filter (true/false/null)—filters notifications by read/unread status if supplied. Null means all statuses are included.

Optional. Lower time-bound for delivered_at—used for filtering results by delivery date (ISO-8601 format).

Optional. Upper time-bound for delivered_at—used for date range filtering.

IDiscussionboardNotification.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for searching and listing notifications for the authenticated member. Supports filters for notification type, read/unread state, and delivery date ranges.

Implements list/search paging according to requirements analysis for notification center implementation. All filtering is governed by API and platform business policy. Returns a paginated, filtered view of notification records as a result.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata object describing the returned window of notifications. Standard system-wide definition, see IPage.IPagination.

data.description: Array of notification records present in the returned page.

IPageDiscussionboardNotification.description:
A page of notification records for the discussion board system. This schema is the standard container structure for multiplexed notification center results, following the pattern set in IPage<T>. Each data element is a single notification object as defined in IDiscussionboardNotification.

The design supports platform-wide consistency in paginated listings and enables UI/UX for notification dashboards and member audit/engagement features.

id.description: Primary key/identifier for the notification record. Ensures every notification event is audit ready and addressable by member and system tools.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member recipient’s unique ID. Enforces 1:1 mapping to user (see notification schema for privacy/audit context).

type.description: Categorical code of notification event (e.g., 'reply', 'mention', 'announcement', 'moderation'). See platform requirements for type enumeration and business logic for handling.

title.description: Notification title/subject, for UI display or inbox/summary preview. Normally a brief description of the trigger event.

body.description: Full textual message of the notification. May contain references to other system elements or member actions.

oneOf.description: Optional. URL or deep-link to related board/forum/thread entity, for use in web/mobile navigation and context restoration.
Optional. URL or deep-link to related board/forum/thread entity, for use in web/mobile navigation and context restoration.

url.description: Optional. URL or deep-link to related board/forum/thread entity, for use in web/mobile navigation and context restoration.

delivered_at.description: Timestamp when the notification was delivered to the member, required for all notification records (ISO-8601 format, UTC preferred).

oneOf.description: Optional timestamp for when notification was read by the member. Null until marked as read.
Optional timestamp for when notification was read by the member. Null until marked as read.

read_at.description: Optional timestamp for when notification was read by the member. Null until marked as read.

created_at.description: Audit timestamp recording when notification was first generated in the system. Ensures traceability, analytics, legal compliance, and debugging capabilities.

IDiscussionboardNotification.description:
Notification event record for the forum system, matching discussionboard_notifications table in the Notifications schema. Each object corresponds to a real notification delivery and includes audit fields required by data governance/business rules.

Comprehensive detail is included, for reliable notification center, engagement analytics, and compliance. The schema enforces a 1:1 mapping for recipient member and tracks title, body, link, delivery/read state, and audit timestamps.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Required. Recipient member's unique ID for whom the notification is being created.

type.description: Categorical event code for notification type (see platform event enumeration and requirements analysis).

title.description: Notification title/subject shown in the member UI notification list.

body.description: Full text or markdown-enabled message body to be delivered.

oneOf.description: Optional. URL or deep-link for notification context (e.g., post, moderation action, thread, announcement).
Optional. URL or deep-link for notification context (e.g., post, moderation action, thread, announcement).

url.description: Optional. URL or deep-link for notification context (e.g., post, moderation action, thread, announcement).

delivered_at.description: Timestamp at which notification should be considered delivered (ISO-8601). May be set in the future for scheduled/batched delivery.

IDiscussionboardNotification.ICreate.description:
Request object for creating a new member notification event per requirements in notification flows and the Prisma schema.

This schema supports both immediate and scheduled delivery. All fields map directly to audit and analytics requirements for system notifications.
