id.description: Primary key/identifier for this settings record. Enforces 1:1 mapping to member via discussionboard_member_id. Required for all retrieval and mutation operations.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Unique member ID to whom these notification settings belong. Foreign key to platform member registry.

in_app_enabled.description: Boolean toggle: true if member is to receive in-app notifications. Controls UI alert pipelining and popups for the member.

email_enabled.description: Boolean toggle: if true, email notifications are sent for matching events.

reply_notification_enabled.description: If true, the system will generate notifications for direct replies to the member's threads, posts, or comments.

mention_notification_enabled.description: If true, enables @mention-based notifications in posts/comments.

moderation_notification_enabled.description: If true, the member will receive notifications regarding moderation events affecting themselves (e.g., warnings, suspensions, content removals).

announcement_notification_enabled.description: If true, system/board announcements will be delivered to this member as notifications.

created_at.description: Timestamp marking when these settings were first created. Used for analytics/audit/compliance.

updated_at.description: Last updated timestamp for these notification settings (ISO-8601 UTC).

IDiscussionboardMemberNotificationSettin.description:
Member’s notification settings object for the DiscussionBoard system, corresponds to the discussionboard_member_notification_settings table in the notification domain schema. Contains full preference flags for each supported event/alert channel as defined by feature requirements and user personalization flows.

All boolean flags are atomic, tracked at the member level, and auditable for compliance, privacy control, and notification workflow optimization.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
ID of the member (UUID) for whom to create notification settings. References the member entity in the database.

This is required for 1:1 linkage and permission enforcement. Ensures settings are applied to the correct user as mandated by privacy and audit requirements.

in_app_enabled.description:
Whether the member wants to receive in-app notifications for activities in the discussion board.

Controls system-side push of new/reply/mention/moderation/announcement events to the web/mobile client UI.

email_enabled.description:
If true, email notifications are delivered for events the member has enabled (e.g., replies, moderation updates, announcements).

Serves for opt-in/opt-out per GDPR and user privacy, fulfills business requirement for alert configuration.

reply_notification_enabled.description:
Whether the member should receive notifications (in-app/email) when someone replies to their posts, comments, or threads.

Implements key engagement flow required for personalized alerting.

mention_notification_enabled.description:
Controls receiving alerts when the member is @mentioned in posts/comments.

Required for engagement and complaint flows as described in user journeys and requirements analysis.

moderation_notification_enabled.description:
Whether the user should receive notifications relating to moderation (warnings, suspensions, moderation actions on their content).

Opt-in/opt-out is required for transparency per business and compliance rules.

announcement_notification_enabled.description:
Indicates if board announcements (global or per-board info, rule changes, etc.) should be pushed to this user.

Field supports member control of communication volume and legal notice requirements.

IDiscussionboardMemberNotificationSettin.description:
Schema for creating a new notification settings record for a DiscussionBoard member.

Implements business requirement for user preference and compliance with privacy regulations. Each property corresponds to toggles in the notification settings UI, giving members granular control over which notifications they wish to receive by channel or event type. All fields are atomic and map directly to the Prisma schema for notification settings records.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
Optionally filters by member ID (UUID). Only retrieve settings for this member if set.

Used in admin dashboards or for analytics.

in_app_enabled.description:
Filter for members who have in-app notifications enabled (true) or disabled (false).

Supports segmentation and delivery targeting.

email_enabled.description: Filter settings where email delivery is enabled/disabled. Used for campaign targeting or opt-out reporting.

announcement_notification_enabled.description: If set, filters members by whether they have enabled announcement notifications. Used for regulatory delivery compliance.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (starts from 1).

Implements standard pagination for list or admin search UI.

limit.description:
Limit on number of results per page (default may be 100 or system-defined cap).

Helps with result batching and API performance.

IDiscussionboardMemberNotificationSettin.description:
Request schema for searching, filtering, or listing DiscussionBoard member notification settings.

Implements query logic as required for user list UIs, admin analysis, and API pagination. Derived directly from Prisma and OpenAPI operation requirements. All properties are optional search/aggregation criteria, with full compliance to original business rules and structure.

data.description: The main list of notification settings records for this response page.

IPageDiscussionboardMemberNotificationSe.description:
Container schema for paginated result sets of DiscussionBoard member notification settings list/search operations.

Follows the IPage<T> convention for OpenAPI pagination. Used for authentication and admin UI endpoints requiring result batching, total count metadata, and standard navigation structure as detailed in business and non-functional requirements.

in_app_enabled.description: Whether the member should receive notifications via in-app delivery. Fulfills UI toggle and opt-in/out flows.

email_enabled.description: If true, email notification delivery is enabled for this member. Supports user self-service for privacy and delivery compliance.

reply_notification_enabled.description: Enable/disable notifications when user receives replies to their posts/comments.

moderation_notification_enabled.description: If true, user will be alerted on moderation events affecting them.

announcement_notification_enabled.description: Whether board announcements are notified to this user.

discussionboardMemberNotificationSetting.description:
Schema for updating the notification delivery preferences for a member in the DiscussionBoard platform.

Used for in-app, email, and per-event-type notification toggles. All fields are optional—updates only supplied properties while preserving other values.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the notification settings record. Primary key in the Prisma schema.

This is required for settings record mutation, lookup, or audit trail referencing.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
UUID identifying the member whom this settings record belongs to. Fulfills 1:1 mapping, linking the settings to an individual user as enforced in the Actors domain data model.

Critical for user-driven preference and privacy enforcement.

in_app_enabled.description:
Indicates whether the member receives in-app notifications for the forum.

Atomic field, maps to personal delivery toggle as per business requirement.

email_enabled.description:
Shows whether email notifications are enabled for this user in the discussion board.

Supports GDPR and user privacy radio toggles in self-service UI.

reply_notification_enabled.description: If true, the member receives notifications on replies to their threads/posts/comments.

moderation_notification_enabled.description: Indicates if moderation action notifications (suspensions, warnings, content edits) are enabled.

announcement_notification_enabled.description: If true, site-wide or board-specific announcements are pushed to this member as notifications.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this notification setting record was created. Set automatically at insert.

Required for compliance and retention audits.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when settings were last updated. Used for audit trails and change history.

Supports rollback/history display in admin tools.

discussionboardMemberNotificationSetting.description:
Main representation of a DiscussionBoard member's notification delivery settings.

Each record is 1:1 tied to a user, with atomic fields for each event/channel toggle. Aligns with business rules for compliance, notification delivery engine, and user-centric opt-in/out control as detailed in the requirements analysis and Prisma schema comments. All fields are mandatory for DB integrity, reporting, and auditability.

id.description: ID of the notification settings record that was deleted. Always present for confirmation and audit trail linkage.

scenario.draft: Test listing and searching for post reports using different filters and pagination options as a moderator/admin. Setup several reported posts from different members, with different reasons and dates. Verify results are returned correctly based on filters such as reporter, target post, date range, and reason. Ensure pagination fields (limit/page) and sorting options work as intended. Confirm that only authorized roles (moderator/admin) can access this endpoint and that regular members are denied access. Also, validate that rate-limits (per-member) do not affect moderators/admins.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple posts in various threads to be reported.
File several post reports by different members against created posts for testing filtering and searching.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the full details of a single post report by its ID. First, create a report as a member. As a moderator or admin, successfully retrieve the report details and ensure all fields are present. As the reporting member, attempt to access the same report and confirm access is granted. Test access with other non-privileged members and verify permission is denied. Validate 404 error for invalid/non-existent report IDs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to be reported.
File a post report to obtain a valid report ID.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a post report by an authenticated member within the allowed daily quota (e.g., 10 reports/day). Prepare a valid post to be reported, submit post reports up to the allowed limit, and confirm each submission succeeds. On the next attempt (exceeding quota), verify that the API returns a quota-exceeded error and prevents additional reports. Also validate input validation and error handling for malformed requests and attempts without member authentication.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as the target for the report.

scenario.draft: Test updating a specific post report as a moderator or admin. Prepare a report, then as a moderator, update the report's resolution state (e.g., mark as resolved or update review status) and verify that changes are persisted. Attempt to update as a regular member (not a moderator/admin) and confirm access is denied. Test error handling for updating non-existent report IDs. All update attempts should follow allowed status transitions as per business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to be reported.
File a post report to get a valid report ID for updating.

scenario.draft: Test deleting (removing) a post report by its ID using both moderator/admin accounts (should succeed) and as an unauthorized/regular member (should fail). Prepare a report, then delete it as an authorized user and confirm successful removal. Attempt deletion with a regular member and verify permission is denied. Validate error handling for deleting an already-deleted or non-existent report (should return proper error responses).

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to be reported.
File a post report to get a valid report ID for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test listing member profiles with different combinations of search, filtering, and pagination options as an admin or moderator. Create several board members with distinct attributes (display name, join date) by registering new members and then creating member profiles for each. Apply filters such as display name search, join date range, and enabled/disabled states. Paginate results and verify accuracy of the returned profiles. Attempt to use filters with no matching records and ensure an empty result set is returned. Validate that only authorized (admin/moderator) users can access this endpoint and that others are denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register multiple new board members to establish distinct users for searching/filtering.
Create at least one member profile for each board member so the endpoint returns results.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a member profile by its unique ID. Begin by creating a new board member, then create a member profile for that member and retrieve it using the profile's ID. Validate the returned details for correctness. Attempt to fetch a profile that does not exist (random UUID) and confirm that a 404 error is returned. Test access control by retrieving another member's profile as a non-admin/non-owner and confirm compliance with privacy/business logic. If profile is linked to a deleted member, ensure error or proper masking per policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board member to link a new profile to.
Create a new profile for the member to retrieve.
(Edge case) Delete the member to whom the profile belonged and test behavior of the GET endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test creating a member profile with valid data. Register a new member, then attempt to create a member profile with proper fields (display name, bio, avatar URI, website, location). Verify that a new profile is created and returned with all provided data. Next, attempt to create a profile when one already exists for the same member and expect a 409 conflict or equivalent error (enforce unique constraint). Verify errors are returned for missing required fields, invalid data (malformed avatar URI/website), and unauthorized access as a non-owner or banned member.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new board member to create a profile for.

scenario.draft: Test updating a member profile with new data. Create a board member and their profile, then update profile details (display name, bio, avatar URI, website, location) as the profile owner and verify updated values. Attempt to update as a different (non-admin, non-owner) user and ensure 403 forbidden response. Test with admin user for elevated privileges. Check for errors if the profile ID does not exist, if attempting updates with invalid data (empty display name, invalid URL), and if profile is soft-deleted or linked to deleted member.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member for profile creation and update.
Create a member profile for testing updates.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting a member profile by profile owner or admin. Register a board member and create their profile. Delete the profile as its owner and verify successful removal (confirmation/status, profile is no longer returned in list or GET). Attempt deletion as a non-owner, non-admin and ensure 403 forbidden response. Delete as admin to confirm elevated privileges. Attempt to delete an already deleted or non-existent profile and confirm appropriate error response. Confirm that deleting a profile affects display in profile listings and does not unintentionally remove associated member data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for the profile to be deleted.
Create a profile for the member to test deletion operations.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of suspension records by moderator or admin. The scenario covers filtering by member ID, moderator ID, status (active, revoked, expired), and timeframe. The test confirms only moderators/admins can access, and that pagination metadata and results adjust according to changing filters. The test also ensures audit trail fields are included and denied access for unauthorized users. Error cases include malformed filters or insufficient privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create regular members to issue and receive suspensions, needed for meaningful filters.
Create suspension records with various attributes (active, revoked, expired) for later filtering.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a suspension record by valid ID for a moderator or admin. Confirm all expected audit, reason, member, and issuer fields are provided. Then, test error handling by attempting to get a record with an invalid or non-existent ID—expect a 404 error. Ensure permission checks deny access for unauthorized users.

dependencies.purpose: Create members for use as suspension targets to obtain suspension record IDs.
Create a suspension record and retrieve its unique ID.

scenario.draft: Test suspension record creation by a moderator or admin for different use cases: (a) single violation, (b) repeat offense, (c) account policy breach. Each scenario ensures the member is suspended successfully, the issuer is properly recorded, timeframe and reason are enforced, and all audit fields are populated. Test failure for privilege violation (non-moderator/admin), attempts to suspend already-suspended members, and missing/invalid request data.

dependencies.purpose: Create regular and moderator/admin members as targets and issuers of suspensions.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing suspension to extend/shorten duration (ends_at), mark as revoked (revoked_at), or correct reason text. Confirm that only moderators/admins may modify, that all updated fields are reflected, and audit logs are consistent. Attempt to update with invalid IDs or as an unauthorized user should fail with clear errors.

dependencies.purpose: Produce members for use as suspension targets and moderators/admins as updaters.
Create a suspension record to be updated in the scenario.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a suspension record by an admin. Upon successful deletion, verify changes in system state and audit log. Attempt deletion as a non-admin, or on an active or non-existent record, to ensure proper error handling. Check that administrative deletion is properly tracked for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Generate members and assign admin role for authorized deletion.
Produce valid and expired suspension records to attempt deletion, covering possible business rule outcomes.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a paginated list of audit logs by an admin user. Send a PATCH request with filter parameters such as action type, actor ID, or date range to retrieve records. Validate that the response contains the expected logs matching the given filters and adheres to pagination and sorting requirements. This tests business logic for advanced log audit capabilities and compliance workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Assign a member as admin so that they have permission to access audit log listing.

scenario.draft: Test failure scenario when a non-admin or unauthorized user attempts to retrieve the audit log list. The request should be rejected with an appropriate authorization error (e.g., 403 Forbidden), ensuring sensitive log data is protected per business and compliance rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member account without admin privileges.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a single audit log record by its unique ID as an admin. Validate that all details match the log entry, including action type, actor, target entity, and timestamps. This is required for investigation or compliance purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure admin privileges for audit log access.
Create an audit log entry to ensure an existing ID for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test behavior when attempting to retrieve an audit log with a non-existent or deleted ID. The system should return a 404 Not Found error, verifying robust error handling for invalid references.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure admin privileges for audit log access.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of an audit log record by an admin user. Provide required fields (action, actor, target entity, details, timestamp) in the request body; validate that the record is stored, all properties are set, and the audit log entry is retrievable in downstream listing and detail endpoints. This ensures logging capability for compliance and tracking exceptional actions.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure the user has admin rights to create audit logs.

scenario.draft: Test audit log creation with missing required fields or malformed data in the request body. The system should reject the request with the appropriate validation error (such as 400 Bad Request), confirming that only well-formed, compliant records can be logged.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure the user has admin rights for create attempt.

scenario.draft: Test update of an audit log record by an admin. Modify fields such as details or classification, then verify that the change is persisted and correctly reflected in retrieval endpoints. All updates should remain fully auditable for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Establish admin privileges for log modification.
Create an audit log entry to update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update an audit log record as a non-admin or unauthorized role. Ensure the operation fails with a 403 Forbidden, enforcing strict modification controls as required for integrity of the audit log system.

dependencies.purpose: Create a non-admin member for the unauthorized attempt.
Create an audit log record to attempt updating.

scenario.draft: Test successful deletion of an audit log record by its ID as an admin user. Confirm that the record is marked as deleted or removed, and that this operation itself is properly logged for compliance, fulfilling business and legal traceability requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Assign a member as admin to perform deletion.
Create an audit log record to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an audit log as a non-admin or unauthorized user. The attempt must fail with a permission error, e.g., 403 Forbidden, ensuring only privileged users can perform such a critical operation. Verify no record is deleted or altered in this case.

dependencies.purpose: Create a non-admin member for unauthorized delete attempt.
Create an audit log entry that will be the target for the failed delete attempt.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of boards with various search and filter options. Verify boards can be listed filtered by category, code, name, and status, and that sorting and pagination (page/limit) options work correctly. Create several boards and categories to populate data; verify that only authorized users see inactive or soft-deleted boards if business rules dictate. Confirm the list result includes accurate metadata, and edge conditions for empty search results or out-of-bounds pagination are handled.

dependencies.purpose: To populate the system with boards for search, filtering, and pagination scenarios. Should be executed before the listing test to ensure test coverage of various board attributes.

scenario.draft: Test successful and failed retrieval of a single board by its unique ID. For success, create a new board and fetch it by its returned ID, verifying all fields (including code, name, category assignment, status, etc). dependencies.purpose: Create a board to provide a valid board ID for successful retrieval and to supply an example of a deletable board for the not-found case.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new board with valid data, ensuring all required fields (name, code, category) are validated and persisted. Also, test failure scenarios: attempt to create a board with a duplicate name/code (verify uniqueness constraint), invalid category reference, or missing required data. Then, attempt updates with invalid data (e.g., duplicate code/name, non-existent category, or forbidden modification of immutable fields), confirming relevant validation errors. dependencies.purpose: Provision a board to update; required for both successful and failed update scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deletion of a board by its ID. Success: create and then delete a board, confirming it is hidden from standard listings but retained for audit. Confirm that dependent discussions or related records are appropriately handled post-deletion based on business policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board that can be soft-deleted in the test. This ensures there is a valid entity for both successful and failed deletion scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to report a comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and the moderator/admin required for update action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to submit and be associated with a report.
Create a comment to be reported.
File a comment report to set up for deletion tests.

dependencies.purpose: Create both recipient and issuer members for the warning creation workflow.

dependencies.purpose: Create member (warning recipient) and moderator (issuer) accounts.

dependencies.purpose: Create member and moderator/admin accounts.

Also cover the edge case where no results match the filters (empty result set).

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a single comment reply relation by its ID. Case 1: Successfully retrieve an existing comment reply and verify returned fields (parent_id, reply_id, member_id, meta). Case 2: Attempt to fetch a reply mapping that was deleted, expecting a 404 error. Case 3: Attempt to fetch a non-existent ID and verify a 404 error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create members who will author comments.
Create at least two comments to use as parent and reply.
Create a comment reply mapping to fetch by ID.
Delete a reply relation to test fetching after explicit deletion (soft/hard depending on business logic).

scenario.draft: Test creating a new comment reply mapping. Case 1: Successfully create a reply mapping between existing parent and reply comments (linked to a valid member). Verify the returned mapping fields. Case 2: Attempt to create a reply mapping with a non-existent parent or reply comment and expect a validation error. Case 3: Attempt to create a reply mapping that exceeds max allowed nesting depth (if enforced by business rules) and expect a rejection. Case 4: Try to create a duplicate reply mapping between the same parent and reply and expect a conflict error or validation failure.

dependencies.purpose: Create members who will author base and reply comments.
Create comments that will act as base nodes for replies.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing comment reply mapping. Case 1: Successfully update a reply mapping by changing its parent_id and verify the update is reflected. Case 2: Attempt to update a mapping to reference a non-existent parent or reply comment and verify a validation or not found error. Case 3: Try to update the mapping to introduce a cycle in the thread hierarchy and validate a business rule error/rejection. Case 4: Attempt to update a mapping with insufficient permissions (wrong member) and expect a forbidden error.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two members for permission/authorization testing.
Create comments for use as parent/reply in mapping.
Create an initial reply mapping for update attempts.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a comment reply mapping. Case 1: Owner or authorized moderator/admin deletes an existing mapping and confirms the correct response. Case 2: Unauthorized member attempts to delete another user's reply mapping and is rejected. Case 3: Attempt to delete a mapping that is already deleted (soft/hard) and verify appropriate error or idempotent success, according to business logic. Case 4: Try deleting a non-existent mapping ID and ensure a 404 error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple members, including one with moderation/admin privileges if required for permission scenarios.
Create comments as base for reply mappings.
Create reply mappings for deletion attempts.

scenario.draft: Test listing board members with pagination and search filters. First, create multiple board members using the member creation endpoint, ensuring various attributes such as different statuses and join dates. Then, as an admin, send a PATCH request with pagination parameters (e.g., page and limit) and search filters (such as searching by a portion of a display name or filtering by status). Assert that the response returns only the matching member records, supports paging across results, and that total count and meta fields are correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create several test member accounts to provide sufficient data for search and pagination results.

scenario.draft: Verify that when a regular (non-admin/moderator) member tries to list members, sensitive fields are not disclosed according to privacy rules. Create two members, one of which is the logged-in user. As a regular member, make a PATCH request and validate that the only returned record is the user's own profile, and that redacted fields are correctly omitted or masked.

dependencies.purpose: Create test member accounts including the logged-in user to validate privacy filters in listing response.
Fetch the details of created users for verifying expected field visibilities.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve the full details of a member's profile by member ID. After creating a new member, execute a GET request as an admin and assert that all non-sensitive and sensitive fields are included in the response, as allowed by admin privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new test member, whose ID will be used in detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Confirm that a regular member can retrieve their own details. After registering a member, use their own credentials to fetch their detail via GET and verify that sensitive/admin-only fields are not present, but all other permitted profile properties are included.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to simulate self-view of profile.

scenario.draft: Check that when a regular member fetches another user's detail by ID, only limited, public profile fields are returned. Register two users, have one request the other's detail, and validate the non-disclosure of sensitive info and proper application of privacy filtering per business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create two distinct test members for checking privacy protections when accessing another's details.

scenario.draft: Simulate a typical member registration using valid data. Provide all required attributes to POST /discussionboard/actors/members. Confirm that the member is created successfully and that the response data matches the input fields, enforcing correct initialization of status, join date, and other required values.

Test registration failure when attempting to create a member with an identifier (e.g., email/username) that already exists. First, register a member with a unique identifier. Then, attempt to register another member using the same identifier and assert that the system returns a duplication/validation error per business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial member record to set up the unique constraint violation scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to register a member providing malformed or invalid data, such as missing required fields or entering an invalid status. Confirm the API validates the input, rejects the registration, and returns appropriate validation error messages.

Test updating a member's status via PUT, simulating an administrative status change (e.g., to 'suspended' or 'inactive'). First, create a member as a test subject. Then, as an admin, update the member's status and verify the status is correctly changed and returned in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member whose status will be updated in the scenario.

scenario.draft: Simulate a regular member updating their own profile fields (e.g., updating display name or profile info). Ensure that only allowed profile fields can be updated by non-admin users. Attempt to update restricted/admin-only fields as a regular member and verify those fields remain unchanged, and that permitted updates succeed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to use for self-update operations.

scenario.draft: Try updating the details of a non-existent member ID and assert that the response is a not-found error. No setup needed for valid member; use a random or already-deleted UUID to simulate the error scenario.

Test that an admin can successfully delete a board member. After creating a member, perform a DELETE as admin and verify that the member is removed, and that related resources such as profiles, authentications, and posts are handled per business rules (cascaded, flagged, or error if not allowed).

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to be deleted during the test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a member as a user who does not have admin rights (e.g., a regular member). Confirm that the API denies the operation and returns an appropriate authorization error, leaving the member unaffected.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member record, and attempt deletion using unauthorized credentials.

scenario.draft: Try to delete a member using a non-existent UUID. Validate that the response is an appropriate error indicating the member does not exist, and ensure no side effects occur for existing data.

Test listing and searching tag proposals as a moderator or admin, with different filters and pagination. Prepare multiple members (some with and some without proposals), and create tag proposals with varying proposed_tag strings and timestamps. Check that filters by string matching, member, date, and status work as intended, and that pagination limits, offsets, and total counts are accurate. Also verify that users without moderation/admin role are denied access or see only allowed data.

dependencies.purpose: Create standard members who will propose tags and have their proposals reviewed.
Insert test tag proposals for various members to establish search and filter variability, testing different strings and scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a tag proposal by its unique ID. First, create several tag proposals using valid members. Retrieve an existing proposal by its valid ID, then try to get a proposal with a non-existent or deleted ID and expect a not found error. Test both as the proposing member and as a moderator/admin (for broader access), ensuring that only permitted users can retrieve details, and others are forbidden (if business logic restricts viewing by non-owners).

dependencies.purpose: Register members to own the tag proposals.
Create tag proposals by those members to get valid proposal IDs for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test creation of new tag proposals as an active member. Attempt to create a tag proposal with a valid and unique tag string; verify success and correct return of the full proposal entity. Next, attempt to propose the same tag again by the same member, expecting an error for duplicate proposal. Also test submitting invalid tag (e.g., containing banned words or not meeting length/content rules) to ensure validation errors are triggered. Finally, attempt to create as a suspended or unauthorized member and validate appropriate failure response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid member to use for proposing a tag.
Suspend a member to test unauthorized proposal attempts.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing tag proposal by the proposing member (owner) and by a moderator/admin. First, create a new tag proposal by a member. Update the proposed_tag value as the owner while it is still under review and confirm the update is applied. Attempt to update it after moderation decision and ensure the business rule blocks further changes. Try updating with invalid data (e.g., duplicates, banned content) and as a non-owner member, expecting errors or forbidden responses. Also verify that moderator or admin can update proposals as per system policy, and all changes are audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Register members for proposing tags and as moderators/admins for performing privileged updates.
Insert tag proposals that will be subsequently updated in different test scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a tag proposal both as the original proposing member and as a moderator/admin. Create a member and submit one or more tag proposals. Delete one of them as the member before moderation review, verifying successful removal. Attempt to delete as a different member and expect forbidden response. As a moderator/admin, delete proposals (even those already under review or reviewed), verifying that business rules on deletion are enforced (e.g., deletion not allowed after review/decision or only by privileged roles). Attempt to delete a non-existent or already-deleted proposal to confirm correct error handling and audit logging of all actions.

dependencies.purpose: Register members to propose tags and as admins/moderators.
Create a variety of tag proposals in different statuses that will be targeted for deletion in the tests.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can search and list moderators using valid filters such as member ID, promotion date, status (active/demoted), and pagination options. Prepare a list of at least two members, promote them to moderators, and query the list using their member IDs and filter for 'active' status. Confirm that only the expected moderator records are returned and that pagination works as intended. This scenario validates business rules for listing moderators, respects pagination/sorting, and tests the admin's search and audit usage.

dependencies.purpose: Create initial member records to be promoted to moderators.
Promote members to moderator to have valid entries for search and filter tests.

scenario.draft: Check that a non-admin user (e.g., regular member) attempting to access the moderator list receives a permission denied (403) response. Create a regular member and attempt to query the moderators list with this user's credentials. This scenario ensures role-based access controls are enforced and audited.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member whose credentials will be used to verify access control for the moderator list.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin or moderator can successfully retrieve the full details of a moderator by providing a valid moderator assignment ID. The test should first create a member, promote the member to moderator, then attempt to fetch their moderator record by ID and confirm all attributes (member, role history, timestamps) are accurately returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member to be promoted.
Promote member to moderator to generate a valid moderator record.

scenario.draft: Test that requesting moderator details with an invalid or non-existent ID results in a 404 Not Found error. Attempt retrieval with a randomly generated UUID that does not correspond to any existing moderator record.

Ensure that a regular member or unauthenticated user cannot retrieve moderator assignment details for another user. Attempt retrieval as a non-admin/non-moderator and check for a 403 Forbidden error, validating RBAC is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member whose credentials are used to verify denied access.

scenario.draft: Confirm that an admin can successfully promote an eligible member to moderator. Register a new member, then call the promote-to-moderator endpoint with valid data. Check that the returned record maps to the member and includes promotion metadata. Also verify side effects such as audit log creation or user notification, if observable through subsequent queries.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member who will be promoted to moderator.

scenario.draft: Validate that promoting a member already holding a moderator role fails due to business logic preventing duplicates. Promote a member to moderator, then attempt to promote again. The endpoint should return an error (typically 409 Conflict or similar).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member.
Promote member to moderator, initial promotion.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to promote a non-existing or invalid member ID fails with the appropriate error (404 Not Found or 400 Bad Request). Attempt the operation using a random UUID or malformed ID value.

Verify that a user without admin privileges (e.g., regular member or unauthenticated) cannot promote someone to moderator. Attempt the operation with such a user and check for a permission denied error (403).

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member for use as a non-privileged subject.

scenario.draft: Confirm that an admin can update a moderator assignment—for example, by setting the demotion timestamp or adjusting privileges. Create a new member, promote to moderator, then update their assignment and check that changes are applied and properly reflected in the returned object. Verify side effects such as audit trail creation.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to serve as the test subject.
Promote member to moderator and obtain moderator role ID.

scenario.draft: Test that updating a moderator assignment with a non-existent or invalid ID yields a 404 Not Found error. Attempt update using a randomly generated UUID or malformed ID.
Ensure that a non-admin or unauthorized user cannot update a moderator assignment. Attempt update as a regular member or unauthenticated user; expect a 403 Forbidden response.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member for use in permission denial test.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully delete (revoke) a moderator assignment by ID. Register a new member, promote the member to moderator, then delete the assignment and verify all privileges are revoked. Also inspect relevant audit or history records where feasible.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member who will be promoted, then unassigned.
Promote member to moderator and obtain moderator role ID.

scenario.draft: Validate that deleting a moderator assignment with a non-existent or already-deleted ID returns a 404 Not Found error. Execute delete operation using an invalid or random UUID not present in the system.

Ensure that a regular member or non-admin user cannot delete a moderator assignment. Attempt the delete operation with regular member's credentials and check for a permission denied error (403), demonstrating RBAC enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member for permission denied scenario.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a paginated suspension list with advanced filters, including by member, issuer role (moderator/admin), active status, and date range. Validate that applicable filters work, pagination returns the correct result set, and access control protects data—non-privileged users should be blocked, authorized users see permitted results. Attempt with various filter combinations to cover edge cases (no results, many pages). Unauthorized access should return 403.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple members to ensure filtration and pagination can be tested, e.g., for 'suspended' and 'non-suspended', issued by different roles.
Seed suspension records for members, issued by moderator and admin roles as necessary for filter diversity.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a single member suspension by valid ID. Verify all fields are correct, including affected member, issuer, reason, period, and revocation status. Confirm only authorized roles (admin, moderator) can retrieve it. Attempting with an unauthorized user should return 403. Attempting to retrieve a non-existent or deleted record should return 404.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to suspend, ensuring there is a known member ID.
Create a suspension for the test member to obtain a known suspension record for lookup.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new member suspension with valid input data (member, issuer, reason, start and end times). Verify that business constraints (cannot suspend already-suspended member, issuer must have privileges) are enforced, and a correct suspension record is returned. Also ensure that audit trails are updated. Attempt various durations and reasons.

dependencies.purpose: Create a normal member as the suspension target.
Create an admin/moderator account as the suspension issuer.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a suspension for a member who is already under an active suspension. The API should reject the request with a duplicate/overlap validation error (typically 409). Ensure the error response contains an appropriate message indicating the member cannot have overlapping suspensions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be suspended.
Create an admin/moderator issuer account.
Issue the initial active suspension for the member.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing member suspension, including modifying the end date to extend/shorten, and the reason message. Ensure that only authorized users (moderator/admin) can perform updates. Attempt valid updates (e.g., extend end date) and check that changes are persisted. Test business rule violations: unauthorized update attempt should give 403, updating immutable fields should fail, invalid ID yields 404. Updates to revoked/expired suspension should be tested for correct error or no-op behavior.

dependencies.purpose: Create both target member and issuer (admin/moderator) for the test.
Create a suspension record to update.

scenario.draft: Test deleting (revoking) a member suspension by ID. Confirm that only the correct roles (moderators/admins) may delete suspensions, and that the action is logged for audit. Check for correct status on a successful delete (204 or defined API response). Attempts to delete with insufficient permissions or a non-existent record must return appropriate errors (403, 404). Verify subsequent reactivation or status updates of the member as applicable by business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to suspend and delete the suspension afterward.
Issue a suspension to the member in order to obtain a valid ID for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can list all global system settings using the PATCH /discussionboard/systematic/settings endpoint, with pagination and sorting applied. Confirm that the result matches expected pagination metadata and includes all relevant settings fields. The admin must be authorized and results should reflect all visible system settings, including those with varied key/value pairs.

Test that an admin can perform a text search and filter the settings list, returning only settings that match a partial key or description. Input: Provide a search term that matches at least one setting. Verify only matching records are returned, and that pagination is correctly applied if the results exceed one page.

dependencies.purpose: Create a system setting with a known key and description for searchability.

scenario.draft: Attempt to list system settings using the PATCH endpoint as a user without admin privileges. Expect a permission denied or forbidden error, confirming access control enforcement.

Test retrieving the details of a system setting by a valid ID as an admin. Should return all properties (key, value, description, timestamps), and the data should match what was created previously via the POST endpoint for settings.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new system setting to ensure a known ID exists for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a system setting's details using an invalid or non-existent ID as an admin. The system should respond with a not found or error status, confirming correct error handling for bad queries.
Attempt to retrieve details of a system setting by ID as a non-admin user. Expect a permission denied error, enforcing administrative access control.

dependencies.purpose: Create a system setting to ensure a valid ID exists to attempt unauthorized access.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new system setting via POST /discussionboard/systematic/settings with a unique key, value, and description as an admin. The setting should be created, persisted, and returned with accurate properties. This test validates correct insertion and audit logging.

Attempt to create a system setting using a key that already exists (case insensitive) as an admin. The system should return an error stating that the key must be unique and not create the record. Confirm that audit logs and error messages reflect the conflict situation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a setting with a target key for duplicate conflict testing.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a system setting as a non-admin user. Expect a 403 Permission Denied or equivalent error, confirming that non-admins cannot add settings.
Attempt to create a system setting as an admin but omit required fields like key or value. The system should respond with a validation error, and the setting should not be created.

Test that an admin can update the value and description of an existing system setting using the PUT endpoint. The setting's key should remain immutable. The result should return the updated object with the new value and audit trail. Initial setup requires creating a setting to update.

dependencies.purpose: Create a system setting to obtain a valid ID for update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a system setting using an invalid or non-existent ID. Expect a not found error, and confirm no update is performed and the system remains consistent.

Attempt to update the key field of an existing system setting (which is documented as immutable). The system should reject the request with a validation error or ignore the key change, returning an error or unmodified key as confirmation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid system setting to attempt an invalid update on the key field.

scenario.draft: Test that a non-admin user cannot update a system setting. Attempt to update any field as a regular member, expect a permission denied error and no update performed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a setting for permission denial testing.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can delete a system setting by its ID. After deletion, the setting should no longer be retrievable by GET and should be persisted as deleted or removed per specification. The audit trail should capture the deletion event.

dependencies.purpose: Create a system setting for subsequent deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a system setting using a non-existent or malformed ID as an admin. The system should return a not found error and not affect any settings.
Attempt to delete a system setting using a valid ID as a non-admin. Expect a permission denied error, and confirm the setting remains available to admins.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid system setting to attempt permission denial scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator or admin can retrieve a paginated and filtered list of post dislikes. Create multiple posts and multiple members. Have various members dislike different posts at different times. Use the PATCH endpoint to filter by post ID, member ID, and date range, and verify pagination/sorting correctness. Check that the results return the correct post dislike entries, and that permission controls prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data fields for non-privileged roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple members to test filtering and permissions across actors.
Create threads required as parents for posts to receive dislikes.
Generate posts to be disliked in the scenario.
Have various members dislike multiple posts, for realistic dataset.

scenario.draft: Test fetching a post dislike by its ID. First, create a member and a post, have the member dislike the post (store the dislike ID). Use the GET endpoint as the liking member and expect full details. Attempt to access the same dislike record with another regular member (not the owner) and ensure access is denied (unless role is moderator/admin). Also test behavior with a non-existent ID (expect 404).

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two members: one to create the dislike, another to test access permissions.
Create a thread as required for post creation.
Create a post to be disliked.
Create a post dislike entry to reference in the test.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can successfully dislike a post they have not previously disliked. Prepare a member and a post, then submit the post dislike and confirm that it is created correctly. Attempt to submit another dislike for the same post and member, and ensure the API returns a uniqueness violation/error (cannot dislike the same post twice).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will perform the dislike action.
Create a thread as the post's parent.
Create a post for the member to dislike.

scenario.draft: Check that a member can update their own post dislike (if business logic allows updating justification or timestamp). First, create a post dislike as a member, then update it with new fields (as permitted), and check the result. Attempt to update a post dislike as another member (non-owner), and ensure that permission error is returned. Also, try updating a non-existent dislike ID and expect a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members to test both owner and non-owner access to updating a dislike.
Create a thread for post creation.
Create the post to be disliked.
Have the member submit a dislike to be updated or tested for permissions.

scenario.draft: Validate that a member can delete their own post dislike, and that authorized roles (moderators/admins) can delete any dislike, while unauthorized users cannot delete other members' dislikes. First, create a post and a corresponding dislike by a member. Delete this as the owner and confirm the record is removed. Re-create the scenario, and attempt deletion as another regular user (should fail), then as a moderator/admin (should succeed). Test deleting a non-existent dislike ID and expect a not found error. Ensure all deletions are audited as per business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create members for testing owner and non-owner deletion scenarios.
Prepare a thread to enable post creation.
Create a post to enable the like/dislike workflow.
Create the post dislike that will be deleted in different roles.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of member authentication records by applying different combinations of filters such as provider type, username/email, and last login timestamp. The scenario should confirm that the search returns only the records matching the applied filters, properly handles pagination, and sorts the results as requested. Also validate that unauthorized access is blocked if restrictions are enabled per deployment. Edge cases should include empty results for unmatched queries and invalid filter values triggering errors. For full coverage, dependencies include creating a member and several authentications with diverse providers/identifiers to ensure plural search results.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more member records to associate with authentication credentials and to enable authenticated search scenarios.
Register authentication records for the created member(s) across multiple providers (e.g., local, OAuth) to provide varied data for search filters.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a specific member authentication record by its unique ID. The scenario should include: (1) successful retrieval of an existing authentication record, (2) attempt to access a non-existent or deleted authentication record (expecting a 404 error), and (3) attempt by an unauthorized user (if applicable) (expecting a 403 forbidden error or equivalent behavior per implementation). Depend on creation of a member and a corresponding authentication record for positive retrieval. The negative cases require both a non-existent ID and a deleted record to test error handling properly.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to serve as the owner of the authentication record(s).
Create an authentication record for the member so that a real UUID is available for lookup by ID.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new member authentication record by providing valid data, including member ID, provider, and unique provider identifier. Cover the case where a duplicate provider/identifier or provider/member pair is submitted (should produce a 403 or 409 error for uniqueness violation). Additionally, attempt to create an authentication for a non-existent member (should produce an error related to referential integrity or validation). Validate that creation logs the new authentication correctly and rejects unauthorized attempts. Dependencies are required to ensure the member exists prior to authentication creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to satisfy referential integrity and supply a valid member ID for authentication creation. This is a required setup for the positive scenario and for testing uniqueness constraints.
Create an initial authentication record to produce duplicate constraint conditions for negative testing.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing member authentication record by replacing all properties (provider, identifier, password hash if applicable, last login info, etc.). Validate success when providing a fully valid dataset, but also cover errors such as attempts to use a provider/identifier pair that conflicts with another authentication record (should trigger a uniqueness error). Attempt updating non-existent records to produce 404 errors. Check permissions if authorization is required for authentication modifications. Dependencies include setting up at least two authentications (for uniqueness testing) and owning member records.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one member to use as the owner of the authentication records.

Create two member authentication records: one for updating, and one for testing uniqueness constraint errors when attempting to update an authentication with a provider/identifier already taken by another entry.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a member authentication record by its unique ID, ensuring: (1) successful soft-deletion by the record's owner or an admin, (2) error response when attempting to delete with insufficient privileges, and (3) error when attempting to delete a non-existent authentication record. After successful deletion, attempting to retrieve the same record should return a not found error. All deletion should be audit-logged. Dependencies include creating a member and at least one authentication record, and possibly elevating a user to admin for role-based tests.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to generate valid authentication credentials and to provide a test subject for delete ownership and permission scenarios.
Create an authentication record that will be a target for deletion, ensuring proper ID linkage for deletion and post-delete retrieval tests.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of categories with various filter combinations. Steps: 1) Create at least two channels and several categories under each, with a mix of enabled/disabled states and parent/child hierarchies (using channel and category creation endpoints). 2) Retrieve categories via PATCH, filtering by channel, enabled status, parent, and/or name substrings. 3) Assert only categories matching filters are returned, pagination and total counts are accurate, and soft-deleted categories are not returned unless business rules allow. Test both admin and moderator access, as required.

dependencies.purpose: Create new channels to assign categories and test channel-based filtering.
Insert new categories—both enabled and disabled, with parent/child structure—to ensure realistic filter combinations.

scenario.draft: Test that only admin and moderator roles can access the category list endpoint. 1) Authenticate as admin, as moderator, and as a non-privileged member. 2) Attempt to retrieve the category list via PATCH as each role. 3) Assert that admin and moderator succeed but a non-privileged user receives a permission error (e.g. 403 Forbidden).

Test successful retrieval of category details by ID and proper error on not found. 1) Create a new category as admin and retrieve its ID. 2) GET the category by ID and verify all returned fields match creation. 3) Attempt to GET a random/nonexistent UUID and confirm the system responds with a 404 error. 4) Optionally, test retrieval of a soft-deleted category as admin and verify correct not found or marked-as-deleted behavior, according to business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category to use its ID for successful fetch scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that only admin and moderator roles can access category details. Attempt to GET a category by ID as an admin, moderator, and regular member. Assert only admin and moderator receive full details, while regular members get a 403 or equivalent access denial.

dependencies.purpose: Category must exist for access control test.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a discussion board category with all required and optional fields. 1) Ensure a valid channel exists (create one if necessary). 2) POST a new category linked to the channel (including parent if testing hierarchy). 3) Assert a success response and verify all attributes are set as requested.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel to provide a valid channel_id for the new category.

scenario.draft: Test failure when creating two categories with the same code within the same channel. 1) Create a channel. 2) POST a category with a given code. 3) Attempt to create a second category with the exact code on the same channel. 4) Assert that the second attempt fails with a uniqueness violation error.

dependencies.purpose: A channel is required to establish channel-scope for uniqueness test.
Create the first category to set up the duplicate scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to create a category with a non-existent channel reference results in a validation error. 1) Attempt to POST a category with a random or invalid channel_id. 2) Assert a validation error indicating invalid or missing channel.
Verify that only admin users can create categories. Attempt to POST new categories as a moderator and as a regular member and expect permission denial errors.

Test successful update of an existing category, as well as validation rules. 1) Create a channel and a category. 2) PUT update the category’s name, code, parent, and enabled status. 3) Assert updates are successful and reflected in returned data. 4) Attempt to change the category code to duplicate another category's code within the same channel and ensure a uniqueness error is raised. 5) Test updating some immutable fields and verify that the API rejects such changes appropriately.

dependencies.purpose: Channels must exist to provide valid foreign keys for update scenarios.
Create initial categories to update and test code uniqueness constraint.

scenario.draft: Test that updating a nonexistent category returns a 404 error. Also, verify that only admins can update categories: attempt updates as a moderator and regular member and expect a 403 or access denied response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new category to allow controlled update attempts and permission checks.

scenario.draft: Test successful soft-deletion of a category and its implications for related entities. 1) Create a channel and category, plus optional boards or topics under that category. 2) DELETE the category as admin. 3) GET the category by ID to confirm soft-deleted state or proper not-found logic. 4) List categories and verify it's no longer returned. 5) Optionally, confirm that related boards/topics are hidden but not physically deleted.

dependencies.purpose: A channel must exist to create a category for deletion testing.
Necessary to create and then delete a category.

scenario.draft: Test that deleting a nonexistent category returns a 404 error. Also, verify that only admins can delete categories—attempt to soft-delete a category as a moderator and a regular member, expecting permission denial errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category to test proper deletion and permission checks.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a list of comments with various filters (by thread ID, post ID, member ID, status, and parent_id), using pagination and sorting arguments. Ensure that authenticated users (member, moderator, admin) see the correct results for their roles: hidden or deleted comments are only visible to staff, while regular members cannot see them. Try combinations where comments are visible, soft-deleted, or made by suspended users, and verify appropriate filtering in the returned response. Validate that pagination and sorting metadata is correctly returned. Edge cases include requesting empty result sets, searching with no matches, exceeding available pages, and invalid filter combinations.

dependencies.purpose: Register or authenticate member and staff accounts needed to test role-specific comment visibility and permissions.
Create comments covering a variety of filterable fields: different posts, members, parent-child nesting, and some soft-deleted or suspended-member comments.
Suspend a member account to verify that their comments appear or are hidden according to system business rules in filtered list results.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a single comment by ID as different authenticated users (author, moderator/admin, unrelated member). Verify the response includes all required fields (body, metadata, relations) when the comment exists and is visible. If the comment is soft-deleted or hidden due to moderation or privacy, validate that access is allowed only to privileged roles. Attempt to fetch a comment that does not exist or is inaccessible due to permissions, ensuring the correct 404 or 403 errors are returned. Edge cases: requesting detail for comments by suspended members, comments belonging to deleted posts, and deeply nested replies.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment that can be retrieved for happy path and soft-delete/error scenarios.
Soft-delete a comment to verify visibility and permission constraints for staff and non-staff users.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new comment as an eligible member on an existing post and as a reply to another comment (by setting parent_id). Validate successful creation, ensuring all required response fields (IDs, timestamps, relations, text) are present. Attempt to create a comment as a suspended user, with an invalid or non-existent post ID, with missing or empty body, or as a reply to a deleted or invalid parent comment—expect appropriate error responses (403 for suspended, 404 for missing target, 400 for validation failures). Business rules such as maximum nesting depth, prohibited content, or exceeding comment quotas should be enforced and tested.

dependencies.purpose: Register or authenticate member accounts, including an active and a suspended user to check for permission and suspension flows.
Create a valid post to comment on and obtain its post ID for comment creation.
Create a parent comment to allow testing for replies/nested commenting limitations and parent-related errors.
Suspend a test member for negative permission validation.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing comment as its author within any allowed edit window, confirming update is successful and response data is correct. Attempt to update as another member (not the author), as a moderator/admin (with elevated privileges), and after the permitted edit window has expired, if applicable. Test forbidden/locked status (such as comments under moderation or deleted). Check for update failures on invalid ID, missing/empty body, or business validation failures (e.g., forbidden content). Validate audit/compliance info is logged and that edit history is accurate if present in schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate member (comment author) and moderator/admin users for permission role testing.
Create a comment that is updated by author and by staff.
Soft-delete or lock a comment to test negative update flows.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting a comment by its author within any allowed window and by moderator/admin accounts with no window restriction. Confirm the deleted_at is set and the comment is hidden for regular users but visible in moderation. Attempt deletion by non-author regular members and when deletion is not allowed (locked, under moderation, already deleted), ensuring the correct error is returned (403 or 404). Edge cases: delete nested/threaded comments, attempt repeated deletion, test audit/logging for deletion actions. Ensure all responses and status fields are handled as described in business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member (author) and moderator/admin accounts as precondition for permission/path checks.
Create one or more comments to serve as deletion targets, including threaded/nested comments for edge case coverage.
Mark or lock a comment as non-deletable for negative test cases (e.g., being reported, root comment for thread, or already deleted).

scenario.draft: Verify successful retrieval of a paginated list of post likes. Simulate the presence of multiple member accounts and posts. Members should like different posts at various times. The test will use filtering (e.g., by member ID, post ID), pagination, and sorting criteria to retrieve a result set, confirming that only matching like records are returned, paginated properly, and sorted as specified. All results must conform to access control and expected metadata structure. Edge case: requesting a page with no records returns an empty result set and correct pagination metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple discussion board member accounts to act as like creators.
Create several posts to serve as targets for like actions.
Have various members like different posts, seeding the like records for query.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a filtered list of post likes using a member ID that does not exist in the system. The API should return an empty list or a clear, documented error message about the member not being found or having no likes.

Confirm successful retrieval of a single post like record using a valid existing like ID. Prepare a post and a member, perform a like action, then request the like record by its ID and assert that its content matches the expected details (member, post, timestamp).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to author the like.
Create a post to be liked.
Have the registered member like the post and obtain the like ID.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a post like record using an invalid UUID or an ID that has been deleted or never existed. The API should return appropriate not found or error responses, and never leak details about non-existent entries.

Test successfully liking a post. Register a member and create a post, then use the API to perform a like. The response should confirm the new like's creation, including all proper fields. Confirm the like is linked to the correct member and post, timestamps are correctly set, and the like does not already exist.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will perform the like action.
Create a post for the member to like.

scenario.draft: Test API enforcement of unique constraints: attempt to like the same post by the same member twice. The API should prevent duplicate likes and return a conflict or appropriate error message. Begin by performing a valid like, then repeat the like action with the same member and post.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for testing duplicate like submission.
Create a post to test duplicate like attempts.
The member likes the post once; setup for duplicate attempt.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a post like where either the member or post does not exist (invalid UUID, deleted resource, or never created). The API should reject the request with a meaningful error, demonstrating validation of member and post existence.

If the schema supports metadata on likes (such as timestamps or notes), verify that the owner (or permitted role) can update mutable fields. Perform an initial like action, then issue an update with changed metadata (avoiding immutable fields like member or post ID if not allowed). Confirm the API correctly updates allowed fields and audit logs the change.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member as the like owner.
Create a post for the like.
Create a like to be updated.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a post like as a member other than the creator, or as an unauthorized/non-privileged user. The API should reject the request due to permission restrictions. Ensure that access control is strictly enforced for sensitive actions.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members: one to create the like, one to attempt the unauthorized update.
Create a post for the like.
Have the first member create a like; second member tries to update it.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a post like record that does not exist (invalid or already-deleted ID). The API should return an appropriate error and not create a new record inadvertently.

Test successful unlike operation by the like's creator. Member likes a post, retrieves like ID, then performs the delete. Confirm the record is removed and engagement metrics are updated accordingly if applicable. Verify audit logging of the action.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to perform like/unlike.
Create a post for like/unlike actions.
Member likes the post; like ID is used for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to unlike (delete) a post like as a member other than the like creator. The API must enforce access controls, preventing non-owners from deleting others' likes and returning a permission denied or forbidden error.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members, one to create the like and another to attempt deletion.
Create a post for both operations.
First member likes the post; second member tries to delete the like.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a non-existent or already-deleted post like. The API should provide a not found or idempotent success response, without side effects or information leakage about previously deleted records or unused IDs.

Test that an admin or moderator can successfully retrieve a paginated and filtered list of content flags. Prepare multiple flagged posts and comments by creating test content and flagging them through the content flag creation endpoint (POST /discussionboard/moderation/contentFlags), some as spam and some as profanity for variety. Verify that the filter (by type, by flagged user, by post/comment ID, by date range) works as intended, only returning content matching criteria. Confirm accurate pagination (page/limit), sorting, and proper error response for out-of-range requests. Also test hidden/deleted/revoked flags do not appear unless specifically requested. Test that unauthorized users receive permission errors when attempting to list flags.

dependencies.purpose: Create a set of flagged posts/comments to ensure there is content to filter and page through. At least two types of flag (e.g., spam, profanity) should be prepared, applied by both regular member and moderator actors.

scenario.draft: Test that regular members or unauthenticated users are denied access (receive a 403 or appropriate error) when attempting to retrieve the content flags list, as only moderators/admins should be authorized. No prerequisites needed other than attempting to call the endpoint with insufficient privileges.

Test that an admin or moderator can successfully retrieve full details of a given content flag by its ID. Create a flag on a test post or comment, then fetch the flag's details using its returned ID. Verify the response includes all expected metadata and references (actor, flagged post/comment, flag type, timestamps).

dependencies.purpose: Create a new content flag to retrieve via GET. Provide a valid post or comment and set an appropriate flag type (e.g., 'spam' or 'profanity').

scenario.draft: Test that a regular member or unauthorized user cannot retrieve details of a content flag due to lack of permissions. Attempt to GET a content flag as a member who is not a moderator/admin and confirm permission is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a flag exists to be tested with an unauthorized access attempt.

scenario.draft: Test that requesting a content flag with a non-existent or deleted flag ID returns a 404 or appropriate error response. Attempt to fetch with a clearly invalid/non-existing UUID.

Test that an authenticated member can create a new content flag on a post. The request should include post ID, member actor, and a valid flag type (e.g., 'abuse', 'spam'). Confirm the flag is stored, the response includes all created fields, and the audit system logs the action. Test variations for flagging by member and by moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will set the content flag.
Create a post to be flagged with the new content flag.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can create a content flag on a comment, using a distinct type such as 'profanity'. Provide moderator credentials, select a comment, and verify the flag is created with correct actor and detail. Also check for trigger of notification systems and audit log entry.

dependencies.purpose: Create both a regular member and a moderator account.
Create a post by the regular member to generate a comment.
Create a comment by the member to be flagged.
Elevate the created member to moderator status.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to create a duplicate flag (same actor, same content, same type) within rate limits or business constraints is rejected. Prepare a flagged post or comment, then attempt to flag again with the same parameters, and verify a suitable error or rejection occurs, in line with deduplication policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member actor for flagging.
Create a post to be flagged.
First, create the initial flag to establish the duplicate condition.

scenario.draft: Test that invalid requests (e.g., missing required fields, both post_id and comment_id provided, or invalid flag type value) fail with proper validation errors. Prepare a working member and test content, then submit malformed requests and assert the error semantics.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid member for flag creation.

scenario.draft: Test that an unauthenticated user or a user with insufficient privileges cannot create a content flag. Attempt to call the endpoint without authentication or proper membership and confirm rejection with a 403 or similar error.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure content exists that could be flagged (e.g., for attempting with a non-member).

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator (or admin) can update the status or type of a content flag (e.g., marking as resolved, reclassifying flag type, updating moderator assignment). Create a flag on a post or comment, then update fields via PUT. Validate that the changes are applied, an audit event is logged, and all business rules are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create member and moderator accounts.
Create a post to be flagged, with comments as needed.
Create an initial flag to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to update a non-existent or deleted content flag ID returns a 404 or suitable error. Attempt PUT with an invalid UUID and check the exact error handling.
