Test that regular members, or users without moderator/admin rights, cannot update flags. Attempt to update as an unauthorized actor and verify proper error response is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member for this scenario.
Create a flag to try to update as a non-privileged user.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin is able to soft-delete a content flag. Prepare a flagged post or comment, then delete it as an admin. Verify the response, confirm flag is marked as deleted and that audit log records the event. Attempt to retrieve the flag after deletion to confirm it is inaccessible or marked deleted as per retention logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and an admin user.
Assign admin role.
Create a post to be flagged.
Create a content flag to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Test that members (without admin/moderator privileges), or unauthenticated users, are denied access to delete a content flag. Attempt deletion and ensure a 403 or appropriate error response is returned for insufficient privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member account for this scenario.
Create a flag record for attempted deletion by non-privileged user.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to delete a content flag with a nonexistent or invalid ID results in a 404 error or suitable error response. Attempt deletion using a UUID not corresponding to any flag in the system and confirm error returned.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of comment dislikes. Scenario should include filtering by comment ID, member ID, and date range, as well as using pagination controls (limit/offset/page). Verify correct records and total counts are returned. Ensure that regular members only see their own dislikes, while moderators/admins can view all records. Test edge cases including invalid filters, requesting out-of-range pages, and requesting when no dislikes exist. Also consider permissions: a regular member should not see other users’ dislikes.

dependencies.purpose: Register members used for creating dislikes and testing filtering by member.
Create comments that will be disliked, necessary for filtering by comment ID.
Create a variety of comment dislikes to set up data for exhaustive listing, filter, and permission tests.
Elevate one user to admin to verify broad access permissions.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a single comment dislike record by its unique ID. Start by creating a comment dislike entry, then fetch it using this endpoint to confirm all expected fields are present and correct. Test for error responses when requesting a non-existent ID and when a user tries to access a dislike they do not own (if not admin/moderator). Verify that admins/moderators can retrieve any dislike record, but regular users can only fetch their own entries.

dependencies.purpose: Register members: one standard, one to be an admin or moderator.
Create the target comment for the dislike action.
Create the comment dislike entry to retrieve.
Promote user to admin for privileged access scenario.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a comment dislike for a valid comment by an authenticated member. Also test business rule enforcement limiting one dislike per member/comment pair by attempting a duplicate dislike (should fail with conflict or validation error). Check error handling for invalid comment ID, member not logged in, and attempts to dislike a comment as a suspended/banned member. Ensure operations are audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Register at least one valid member, and a second for duplicate test.
Create a comment to be disliked.
Optionally, suspend a member to test permission/validation restrictions on dislike creation.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing comment dislike (e.g., changing the associated comment if allowed, or updating timestamp if logic permits) by the like owner and by an admin. Ensure only owners or privileged users can update records; others receive a permission error. Confirm the update is reflected in returned data, and all changes are audit logged. Attempt to update a non-existent dislike and verify error response.

dependencies.purpose: Register both owner and admin users.
Create at least two comments (one for the original dislike; another if updating comment reference is supported).
Create a comment dislike to serve as the target for updates.
Promote a user to admin for elevated update tests.

scenario.draft: Verify that a member can delete their own comment dislike, and that privileged users (admin/moderator) can delete any dislike. Test attempts to delete another user's dislike as a regular member (should fail with permission error). Validate deletion of a non-existent or already deleted record returns appropriate error. Ensure deletion is audited and the dislike can be recreated for the same comment/member pair afterward (i.e., business rule on re-allowing dislike after delete).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member and an admin user.
Create a comment to be disliked.
Create a dislike record for deletion tests.
Set up admin account for privilege test.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a paginated, filtered list of moderation reports. First, create a member and trigger one or more reports (e.g., by reporting an inappropriate post or comment). Then, as a moderator or admin, call the moderation reports list endpoint with various search filters such as status (pending, reviewed), timestamps, reported member IDs, and verify that returned results are correctly filtered, paginated, and sorted. Validate correct access control: only moderators or admins may retrieve the list. Edge case: test access with unauthorized roles (e.g., regular member) and ensure access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts to act as legitimate reporters or reported members in the moderation flow.
Trigger at least one report to ensure data exists for pagination/search, and to use specific statuses or targets.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a moderation report's full detail by its ID. First, create a report (as a member) on a post or comment. Then, as a moderator/admin, call the GET endpoint with the report ID and verify all fields are correctly returned (target, reason, resolved status, etc.). Validate access control, ensuring only privileged roles can view. Edge case: request a report with an invalid or non-existent ID and check for proper error response. Also, attempt to access as an unauthorized regular member and expect permission denial.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be the report submitter and/or the reported party.
File a report to obtain a valid report ID for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a moderation report for both post and comment scenarios by a member. Validate success on providing all valid and required fields (reason, target entity). Also, test business rule enforcement: ensure a user cannot exceed daily quota for report creation (e.g., 10 per day), and attempt invalid input such as missing required fields or referencing a non-existent target, verifying appropriate error responses. Confirm that only authenticated, eligible members may create reports, and calls by guests or suspended users are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a legitimate member account to submit reports. This is also useful for quota edge case by creating multiple reports.
Create a post as potential reporting target for the report API.
Create a comment as alternative reporting target to test both report types.
Update a member's status to suspended to validate denial of report creation for suspended/blocked accounts.

scenario.draft: Test updating a moderation report (e.g., changing status to reviewed, assigning a resolver/moderator, or updating resolution fields). First, create a member and a report entry. Then, as a moderator/admin, invoke the PUT endpoint to update various report fields. Verify that the updates are reflected correctly and are audit-logged if required. Edge case: attempt modification of immutable fields, invalid transitions, or by users without sufficient privilege, and check that proper errors are returned. Also, try updating a non-existent report and confirm appropriate error feedback.

dependencies.purpose: Create accounts for reporting and moderation roles.
Create a report record to act as target for update operations.

scenario.draft: Test the workflow for deleting a moderation report. Prepare by creating a report via a member, then as a moderator or admin, attempt deletion and verify successful removal (could be soft or hard per business rules). Validate that only authorized roles can delete; attempts by unauthorized users (e.g., regular members) must fail. Edge cases: try to delete a non-existent or already-deleted record and confirm suitable error response. For compliance, verify deletion is correctly audit-logged if policy requires.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare legitimate member identities for test setup.
Create a report entry to be deleted in test.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of post attachments for posts in the discussion board. The scenario starts by authenticating as a member who has previously created posts and uploaded attachments. Attachments must have diverse metadata: different file names, file types (image, document), uploaders, and timestamps. Use the endpoint to filter by post, file type, uploaded_by, and verify pagination works correctly. Ensure that permission rules apply: only authors, thread participants, moderators, and admins can view specific files; attachments tied to posts not accessible to the user must not appear. Attempt searching with invalid filters (e.g., unauthorized post or invalid pagination parameters) and check for correct error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to use as uploader and thread participant.
Create threads as authorized member to generate post contexts for attachments.
Create posts within threads, as the target for uploading attachments.
Upload various attachments to posts, diversifying file types, uploaders, and timestamps for filter/pagination testing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving full metadata for a post attachment by its ID. Authenticate as the uploader and as a different member (both a thread participant and a non-participant). Create an attachment on a test post and ensure the uploader can successfully retrieve its metadata, including file name, file type, and upload info. As another thread participant, confirm access is permitted. As a non-participant with no rights, confirm access is denied or returns proper permission error. Test behavior when requesting a non-existent or deleted attachment ID: should return not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts (the uploader and the 'other user').
Create a discussion thread and associated post for attachment.
Create a post as the uploader within the thread.
Upload an attachment to a post to serve as lookup target.

scenario.draft: Test uploading a new file attachment to an existing post by an authenticated user. Begin by authenticating as the post author. Upload a file (satisfying allowed file type, file size, and format constraints). Verify the returned data accurately reflects the uploaded file's metadata. Next, test edge/failure cases: attempt upload as a member who did not author the post, upload with an invalid or oversized file, or upload using an invalid post ID. Ensure proper error responses for permission, validation, or missing post. Try to exceed any upload quota for the member and check rate limit errors if applicable.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member for post author identity.
Create a thread as setup for the test post.
Create a post as this member to be used for attachment uploads.

scenario.draft: Test updating metadata of an existing post attachment. Authenticate as the uploader and as a moderator/admin. Attempt to modify metadata such as file name, file type, or description for a post attachment. Verify the owner and authorized staff are able to update successfully and changes are reflected accordingly. Attempt update as an unauthorized member and expect a permission error. Validate business logic prevents updating a deleted or non-existent attachment, returning correct errors. Edge case: try to change file type to a forbidden value or violate file property constraints and check for validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as uploader and one as unauthorized member.
Create a thread for post/attachment context.
Create a post linked to the attachment.
Upload an attachment to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test deleting (soft-deleting) a post attachment. The scenario begins by uploading an attachment, then deleting it as the uploader, verifying successful deletion and that the record is marked as deleted but preserved for compliance. Next, attempt to delete the same attachment as an unauthorized member and expect a permission denied error. Test moderator/admin can delete any attachment. Try deleting an already deleted or non-existent attachment to verify proper error response. Confirm that after deletion, the attachment is not accessible to regular users, but audit history is retained for moderators/admins.

dependencies.purpose: Create authorized user (uploader) and unauthorized member, with additional moderator/admin as needed.
Create a thread as context for the post.
Create a post for testing attachment upload and deletion.
Upload the attachment to target for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a paginated, filtered list of moderation action logs as a moderator or admin. Admin should be able to specify filter criteria such as the moderator ID, action_type, affected entity, and time range in the request body. The scenario should validate: (1) correct filtering of results according to criteria; (2) that results are paginated properly using limit/offset or page/cursor as specified; (3) that only users with at least moderator privileges can access this endpoint, while unauthorized roles (e.g., a regular member or unauthenticated user) receive a 403 (forbidden) error. Edge cases: query with no matching filters should return an empty result set with correct pagination meta; malformed filters or exceeded paging limits should return appropriate error codes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a base member account to later promote to moderator/admin for elevated privileges.
Promote the base member to an admin to perform log queries as an authorized user.
Create multiple moderation log entries to populate the logs for filtered queries.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a specific moderation log entry by ID by a moderator or admin. First, as an admin, fetch the log using a valid log ID to verify that the returned object matches expected audit data. Then, attempt to access a non-existent log entry (e.g., random UUID) and verify a 404 not found error is returned. Attempt to access a valid log as a regular member or unauthenticated user and confirm a 403 forbidden error. This ensures permission enforcement and error handling for invalid ID or role.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to later promote and test admin-level access.
Promote a member to admin so they can access the log details.
Create a moderation log entry to retrieve using its ID.

scenario.draft: Verify that authorized moderators or admins can create a new moderation action log via this endpoint. Provide valid log data including moderator ID, action type, details, and target entity (e.g., post, comment, or member). Confirm that the operation succeeds, the returned log object matches the posted data, and that the entry appears in subsequent log listings. Attempt log creation using a regular member or unauthenticated user and assert that a 403 forbidden error is returned. Edge case: attempt invalid or incomplete input payload, confirm validation error (400 Bad Request) is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member, to later promote to moderator or admin for log creation.
Promote the member to admin so they can create log entries.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing moderation log entry as admin (and, if business rules allow, as a moderator). Provide a new action detail (such as updated description or corrected target reference) and validate that the response contains the updated data. Attempt to update a non-existent log entry and confirm a 404 error. Attempt the update as a regular member and verify access is denied (403 forbidden). Also, deliberately send an invalid payload (e.g., missing required fields) to ensure a 400 Bad Request is returned for validation errors. Updates to immutable audit fields (if present) should be rejected according to business constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member, to later promote to admin for update permissions.
Elevate the member to admin for performing update action.
Create a moderation log entry to update during the test.

scenario.draft: Validate that an admin can delete a moderation log entry by specifying its ID. Ensure the operation properly soft/hard-deletes the log (depending on business rules) and that deleted entries are inaccessible from subsequent GET requests. Attempt deletion as a non-admin (moderator or member) and confirm permission is denied (403 or equivalent error). Also, attempt to delete a non-existent (random) log ID and check that a 404 is returned. After successful deletion, verify an audit trace of the deletion event is created as required by compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member, to be promoted to admin for deletion permissions.
Promote the member to admin so log entries can be deleted.
Create a moderation log entry to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of channels as an authenticated admin. Prepare the system with several channels containing various enabled states, names, and descriptions. Use the endpoint with search terms, filters (enabled/disabled), and pagination options. Validate that results match filter criteria, pagination works as expected, and all necessary channel data appears. This scenario targets a typical admin dashboard usage pattern.

dependencies.purpose: Seed the system with multiple channels of varying properties and enabled states before listing.

scenario.draft: Test that a non-admin or non-moderator cannot access the list channels endpoint. Attempt to call the endpoint as a regular member or unauthenticated user and ensure access is denied with the proper error code.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member account to use for attempting endpoint access.

scenario.draft: Test that channels marked as soft-deleted (deleted_at set) are hidden or indicated as deleted unless explicitly requested. First, create multiple channels, then soft-delete one. List channels and verify the deleted channel is handled according to the filter, either excluded, or present but marked.

dependencies.purpose: Create channels for initial state.
Soft-delete one of the previously created channels to setup for the test.

scenario.draft: Test successfully retrieving a channel's complete details by its valid ID as an admin. First, create a channel, then retrieve by the returned ID and verify all properties (name, code, description, enabled, timestamps, relations) are present and correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel and obtain its ID for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving channel details with a non-existent or invalid ID. Attempt to fetch a channel using an ID not present in the system (e.g., random UUID) and verify a not found error is returned.

Test that retrieving a soft-deleted channel returns an appropriate error or includes a deleted flag. Create and soft-delete a channel, then attempt to get its details as an admin and verify the system behavior matches business rules for soft-deleted entities.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel to be soft-deleted.
Soft-delete the newly created channel.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new channel as an admin with all required valid fields (unique code, name, set enabled, etc). Check that the newly created channel matches input, appears in listings, and is auditable.

Test failure to create a channel with a duplicate code or name. Create an initial channel, then attempt to create another with the same code or name. Verify the endpoint returns an error indicating uniqueness constraint violation.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a baseline channel with a specific code and name for later duplication attempt.

scenario.draft: Test that omitting required channel fields (e.g., code, name) results in validation errors. Attempt to create a channel with missing or null required fields and verify proper error response.

Test that non-admin users (e.g., moderator, member) cannot create channels. Attempt to create a channel while authenticated as a moderator or normal member, and verify a forbidden/authorization error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular user for negative permission testing.

scenario.draft: Test updating a channel's details as an admin with valid inputs (change name, description, enabled state, etc). First, create a channel, then update its attributes and verify the changes persist and audit logs are created.

dependencies.purpose: Setup by creating a channel to update.

scenario.draft: Test that updating a channel to use a code already assigned to another channel fails. Create two channels, then attempt to update one with the other's code, verifying a uniqueness constraint error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create two channels with unique codes to test conflict.

scenario.draft: Test that a non-admin (moderator, member) cannot update a channel's properties. Attempt to update a channel as a non-admin and verify permission is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel for negative permission testing.
Create a regular member user to try updating channel as non-admin.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when trying to update a non-existent channel. Attempt to update with an invalid or missing ID and verify a not found error is returned.

Test soft-deleting a channel as an admin. Create a channel, perform the soft-delete, then verify it no longer appears in default listings, deleted_at is set, and dependent data is appropriately hidden. Ensure proper audit logging of the action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel to be soft-deleted.

scenario.draft: Test that a non-admin cannot soft-delete a channel. Attempt to soft-delete an existing channel as a moderator or regular member, verifying the correct authorization error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel for the deletion attempt.
Create a regular member user who will attempt to delete the channel.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to soft-delete a channel with an invalid or non-existent ID returns not found or appropriate error.

Test listing and searching comment likes using a variety of filter criteria, such as specific member ID, comment ID, and time window. Ensure pagination (page/limit) and sorting options work as expected. Admin/moderator should be able to retrieve full datasets while regular members can only access their own records. Confirm results match expected query, and that permissions are properly enforced. Edge case: request with out-of-range or invalid parameters should return appropriate error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create members whose comment engagements will be tested.
Create comments to receive likes, referenced in search tests.
Seed likes for various members/comments for realistic query conditions.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a single comment like by a valid ID (should succeed) and an invalid/nonexistent ID (should yield correct error, such as 404). Check that only the liking member, moderator, or admin can access the record details; attempt forbidden access as other members to verify enforced permissions. Business rule: ensure audit/logging where details are potentially sensitive.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for like creation and permission checks.
Create a comment for the like operation.
Like a comment (to generate a valid like ID).

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a comment like by an authenticated member on a comment, then attempt a duplicate like on the same comment by the same member (should fail with a duplicate/constraint error). Verify attempts to like as an unauthenticated user or for nonexistent comments are rejected. Ensure audit trail is generated for creation and error cases.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to perform like actions.
Create a comment on which like will be created.

scenario.draft: Test update of a comment like by: a) the liking member (should succeed), b) moderator/admin (should succeed), c) a different member (should fail with permission error). Attempt update with non-existent like ID (should 404). Changes should be reflected, and all updates must be tracked in audit logs for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple member accounts representing actors (owner, non-owner, admin/moderator for permission checks).
Create a comment to like and update.
Create the initial like record to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deletion (unlike) of a comment like by: a) the like's creator (should succeed), b) an admin or moderator (should succeed), c) an unrelated regular member (should fail with permission error). Attempt to delete a non-existent or already deleted like (should yield 404 or appropriate error). Deletion must be audit-logged and accurately reflected in the like counts for the comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create members for like ownership and permission scenarios.
Create comment for like and future deletion action.
Create a comment like to later test deletion scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a member's notification settings by providing a valid settings ID. Ensure that the requesting user is either the owner (the member themselves) or an admin. Validate that the result includes the current preferences for all notification types and channels. This scenario requires creating a member, logging them in, and creating their notification settings first.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member who will own the notification settings.
Create initial notification settings for the registered member to generate a valid settings ID.

scenario.draft: Attempt to fetch another member's notification settings as a different regular member (not admin). Expect a 403 error or equivalent insufficient permission result. Precondition: Two members must exist, with one serving as owner and the other as unauthorized accessor.

dependencies.purpose: Create two separate member accounts.
Create notification settings for the owner member before attempting unauthorized access.

scenario.draft: Attempt to fetch notification settings using a non-existent or invalid ID (random UUID not linked to any settings). Expect a 404 error or resource not found response. This tests the system's error handling for missing resources.

Test creating a new notification settings record for a member upon onboarding, providing valid and complete preference information. The scenario should assert that duplicate settings for the same member cannot be created and should validate successful creation response. Requires member account creation prior to test.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member whose notification settings will be managed.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a notification settings record for a member who already has one. Expect a 409 conflict error or equivalent. This verifies the business rule that only one settings record per member is allowed.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account.
Establish existing notification settings for this member before attempting a duplicate creation.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can create notification settings for another user's account (e.g., managed/enterprise accounts). Validate authorization and result. Requires an admin and a regular member account.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to be managed.
Create or elevate a user to admin role before attempting to create settings as admin.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve a filtered and paginated list of notification settings for multiple members. Use search filters such as notification type enabled status or member ID. Validate that the results are paginated and contain only records matching the filters. Requires creation of several member records and notification settings.

dependencies.purpose: Create several member accounts to populate test data.
Create notification settings records for each member for testing the listing operation.
Assign admin privileges to a user to perform the list operation.

scenario.draft: Attempt to list notification settings with a regular member account. Expect a 403 forbidden or equivalent error result. This validates access restrictions for this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to attempt the unauthorized list operation.

scenario.draft: Test updating notification settings as the member who owns them. Change multiple preferences (e.g., enable/disable email alerts, replies, etc.) and confirm the updates are persisted. Owner authentication must be ensured. Precondition: Member and settings must exist.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will own and update their notification settings.
Create notification settings for this member before performing update.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can update notification settings on behalf of another member. Change some preferences and ensure changes are successful and logged. Requires both admin and regular member accounts and pre-existing notification settings for the member.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member whose settings will be updated.
Create or assign an admin to perform the update.
Create notification settings for the member prior to update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a different member's notification settings as a regular member (not admin or owner). Expect a 403 forbidden error or equivalent. Both members and the settings must be established first.

dependencies.purpose: Create two regular members for ownership and unauthorized update attempt.
Create notification settings for the target member.

scenario.draft: Test successful deletion of a member's own notification settings. The owner authenticates, requests deletion, and the operation completes with verification that the record is gone or access now returns not found. Precondition: Member and settings created.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will own the notification settings.
Create a notification settings record for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test admin user successfully deleting another member’s notification settings (e.g., for compliance or account closure). Admin authentication/authorization must be used. The deleted settings should no longer be retrievable after this action. Precondition: Admin and member accounts, with settings established.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member whose settings are to be deleted.
Assign or elevate admin user for privileged deletion.
Set up notification settings to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete another member’s notification settings as a non-owner, non-admin. This should return a 403 forbidden error, confirming that only the owner or admin can delete notification settings. Requires multiple member accounts with settings.

dependencies.purpose: Create two regular members: one as the owner and another as the unauthorized deleter.
Create notification settings for the target (owner) member.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a paginated list of admin assignments using combinations of search filters such as member ID, date range, and status. Scenario includes verifying basic pagination (page/limit), combination filters, and sorting. Verify that only authenticated users with admin privileges can access full admin assignment details. Check response format, pagination metadata, and data sensitivity (e.g., member info exposure).

dependencies.purpose: Assign one or more members as admins to ensure there are admin assignments to be retrieved in the listing test. Create relevant member records if necessary by calling the registration endpoint first.
Create basic member records so they can be promoted to admin for assignment testing.

scenario.draft: Test that non-admin users are denied access to the admin assignment listing endpoint, receiving a clear error response (such as 403 Forbidden). Attempt to list admin assignments while authenticated as a non-admin member and as an unauthenticated user, and verify proper error messaging.

dependencies.purpose: Register a standard non-admin member who will attempt to access the admins listing. Use this account for the denial case.

scenario.draft: Test fetching the details of a specific admin assignment using a valid assignment ID as an authenticated admin. Validate that all fields are present and accurate, including member linkage, permission info, and timestamps. This scenario ensures correct data retrieval and role-based access control.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin assignment to obtain a valid ID to retrieve in this test.
Create a member who will be promoted to admin, providing the underlying assignment record.

scenario.draft: Test fetching the details of an admin assignment using an invalid or non-existent ID. Confirm the system returns an informative not found error, with no sensitive data leaked. Attempt as both admin and non-admin users.

Test that non-admin users (e.g., standard members) are denied access to admin assignment details, receiving a 403 Forbidden or equivalent error response. Attempt retrieval with a member session and as unauthenticated client.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member account to use for the permission-denied test.

scenario.draft: Test successful promotion of a member to admin when the member is eligible and caller is a current admin. Validate that audit logs are triggered, notification is sent if relevant, and the resulting assignment record reflects the correct member with proper timestamps. Confirm correct linkage between member and admin assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member eligible for promotion to admin.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to promote a member who is already an admin yields an appropriate error (e.g., conflict or duplicate error), preventing double assignment. Confirm the error is returned and no new assignment is created.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member and promote them to admin (using POST /discussionboard/actors/admins) first, in order to trigger a duplicate scenario.

scenario.draft: Test promoting a member to admin with a non-existent or malformed member ID. Expect a validation or not-found error. Validate error messaging and appropriate handling without side effects.

Test successful update of an existing admin assignment by ID, adjusting privileges or metadata (e.g., demotion, notes). Verify that changes are reflected in the assignment, that only admins can perform the update, and that an audit log entry is generated as required. Validate all updated fields are stored as per schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be promoted to admin for setting up the admin assignment record.
Assign the admin role to the member, so there is an assignment to update.

scenario.draft: Test that a non-admin user cannot update an admin assignment. Attempt to update using both a regular member's credentials and as an unauthenticated user. Expect permission denied (403) or similar error, with no changes made.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member to use for the test.
Establish an existing admin assignment to attempt unauthorized update.

scenario.draft: Update an admin assignment using a non-existent or malformed ID. Confirm the system returns a clear error response and does not perform any updates.

Test successful deletion (revocation) of an admin assignment using a valid ID as an authenticated admin. Confirm that admin privileges are properly revoked and audit logs record the change. Also, ensure that removal cannot occur if it would violate business rules (e.g., deleting the last admin).

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will be promoted to admin for the deletion test.
Create an admin assignment to delete during test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an admin assignment with a non-existent or malformed ID. Expect an informative not-found or validation error response.

Verify that only authenticated admins can delete (revoke) admin assignments. Attempt deletion as a standard member and as an unauthenticated user, and verify permission is denied with no assignment actually revoked.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for attempting the unauthorized delete.
Ensure an admin assignment exists so the member can attempt (and fail) to delete it.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve a paginated list of threads with filters (e.g., by board, creator, or status). First, authenticate as an admin. Create two boards and several threads with different statuses, creators, and creation times to set up diversity. Request a list of threads with specific filters such as board ID, status (e.g., 'open'), or searching by thread title, asserting that only matching threads are returned. Test sorting and pagination by requesting only a subset of results and checking the metadata. Consider edge cases: no matching threads, empty result set, and querying after some threads are soft-deleted. Ensure appropriate error is returned if authentication is absent or role insufficient.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple boards to use as thread targets for filter diversity.
Create several threads with different combinations of creator, status, and board for realistic filter testing.
Soft-delete a thread for negative filter cases (e.g., ensure deleted threads are not returned unless explicitly requested, if supported).

scenario.draft: Test that a suspended member cannot retrieve threads or receives only restricted results. First, create a regular member and suspend them via the suspension endpoint. Attempt to retrieve the thread listing while authenticated as the suspended member, asserting that the operation is denied or returns an appropriate error/status per business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member who will be suspended.
Suspend the member to restrict thread access.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of detailed thread info by ID. First, create a new thread as a regular member and store its thread ID. Retrieve details for this thread and verify all attributes (title, description, status, creator, etc.) are correctly populated. Then, attempt to fetch a thread with a random, non-existent UUID and assert that a 'not found' error or the correct error code is returned. Also, soft-delete the thread and confirm the error or status when trying to fetch a deleted thread (visibility per role).

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member for thread authorship.
Create a thread to get a valid thread ID.
Soft-delete the thread and verify retrieval behavior post-deletion.

scenario.draft: Ensure that thread details are only retrievable by users with adequate permissions according to system visibility and thread status (e.g., locked/hidden threads may have restrictions). Create a thread, then simulate scenarios where the thread is visible, hidden, or locked. Try to retrieve the hidden or locked thread as various roles (member, moderator, admin), verifying correct access control enforcement. Edge: suspended users may be blocked from viewing certain threads.

dependencies.purpose: Create members with different roles as required for permission scenarios.
Create threads that will later be locked/hidden.
Update thread status to simulate locked or hidden state for testing permission boundaries.

scenario.draft: Test creation of discussion threads by authenticated members. Register a member, create a board, then create a thread providing required and optional fields (title, description, board ID, etc.). Check response for all attributes and that audit logging occurs. Also attempt thread creation with missing required fields (such as title or board ID), invalid (non-existent) board or member, or while the member is suspended, asserting that appropriate validation or business rule violations result in structured errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for thread authorship.
Create a board to attach the new thread to.
Suspend a member to confirm suspended users cannot create threads.

scenario.draft: Ensure that creating a thread with a title or code that already exists within the same board fails with a duplicate error. Register a member, create a board, and create an initial thread with a specific title in that board. Attempt to create a second thread (same board) using the same title or code and assert that a conflict/uniqueness violation is enforced by the API.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for thread authorship.
Create the target board.
Create the initial thread to set up the duplicate constraint.

scenario.draft: Check updating threads with various scenarios. Create a thread (member), then update its title, description, or status, verifying correct changes are returned. Confirm audit logging of updates. Also test errors: update as an unauthorized user (non-creator, or after suspension), invalid status transitions (e.g., locking/unlocking thread as regular member), and updating a non-existent or deleted thread. Verify system enforces access and business logic strictly.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as the author for thread creation and for role-based checks.
Board for the thread.
Create a thread to obtain a valid ID.
Use deleted thread to check update error handling.

scenario.draft: Validate soft-deletion of threads. Author creates a thread, then deletes it and checks that it is flagged as deleted (not physically removed), is hidden for regular users, but still accessible to admins/moderators for audit. Test errors: deleting a non-existent, already-deleted, or another user's thread without proper role. Attempt deletion by a suspended user and verify permission denied. Confirm that all deletion events are logged for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create members for author and role tests.
Create a board for thread placement.
Create thread for deletion.
Attempt re-deletion or test deletion on already deleted thread for error scenario.

scenario.draft:
Test that an admin or moderator can retrieve a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of moderator actions using various search criteria such as moderator ID, action type, target type, and a time range. The scenario should verify that correct filtering, sorting, and pagination are applied and that only actions available to the authenticated role are shown. Edge cases include requesting with restrictive filters yielding empty results, and combining multiple search parameters. Unauthorized roles should receive a 403 forbidden error.

Dependencies:
1. Ensure a moderator/admin exists via member and assignment creation endpoints.
2. At least one moderator action log exists—either created by real moderation activity or directly using the create endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Assign an admin to have the correct privileges for listing moderator actions. Must be done before searching for actions to ensure role validity.
Create at least one moderator action record to provide data for the list/search scenario.

scenario.draft:
Test retrieving a moderator action log by its ID. Scenario includes successful retrieval by an admin or moderator and handling a 404 error if the action does not exist. It should also validate permission—unauthorized users must be denied access. The retrieved data must contain all fields including moderator info, context, and timestamps, matching the record created.

Dependencies:
1. Create a moderator/admin user and assign necessary roles.
2. Create a moderator action log entry and use its ID for retrieval.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a user is assigned as admin for proper privilege to access action logs.
Create a moderator action log entry to generate the test ID for retrieval.

scenario.draft:
Test creation of a new moderator action log entry by a moderator or admin. It covers successful log creation with all required fields (moderator, action_type, target_type, target_id, details, timestamp) and verifies that the returned record matches the provided data. Negative cases include attempting to create a log as an unauthorized user (should result in 403), omission of required fields, or invalid references (e.g., non-existent moderator ID). 

Dependencies:
1. Create a member and promote to moderator/admin to have a valid issuer for the action log.
2. Prepare a relevant target entity (such as a post, comment, or member) that can be referenced by target_type and target_id.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to promote as moderator/admin, which is required for creating a moderator action log.
Promote a member to moderator so the log can reference a valid moderator.
Create a post or entity that can act as a valid moderation target for the action log's target_id field.

scenario.draft:
Test updating an existing moderator action log entry with new details, including changing the justification (details field), adjusting target information, or correcting a timestamp. Success path: moderator/admin successfully updates the action log and all changes are reflected accurately. Error scenarios: updating non-existent action log (404 error), unauthorized update attempts (403 error), or providing invalid update data. All updates must be properly audit-logged and restricted to valid fields only.

Dependencies:
1. Assign moderator/admin role to the acting user through creation and promotion APIs.
2. Create a moderator action log to be updated; use its ID for the update scenario.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator/admin privilege so user has authority to perform updates on moderator action logs.
Create a moderator action log record for the update test.

scenario.draft:
Test deleting (anonymizing) a moderator action log entry by its ID. A successful case will result in the log becoming inaccessible or status-confirmed. Verify required permissions: only moderators/admins can delete; others receive a 403 error. Also, test deletion of a non-existent record (404 error). All deletions should be audit-logged for compliance.

Dependencies:
1. Promote a test user to moderator/admin for proper deletion permissions.
2. Create a moderator action log to generate a valid ID for deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin privileges to the acting user to validate permission-controlled deletion.
Create a moderator action log so there is a log entry to delete during the test.

scenario.draft: Test fetching a paginated and filtered list of board topics. First, create a board (requires admin). Then, create multiple topics under that board using different codes and titles (by members). Finally, invoke the topics listing endpoint with search criteria such as filter by board ID, keyword search (on title), and pagination arguments (page/limit), and verify the correct set of topics is returned with accurate metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new board to associate board topics with. Required before topic creation.
Create several board topics across one or more boards to populate data for the listing test.

scenario.draft: Test that requesting topics for a board ID that does not exist returns an empty list, not an error. Create a unique non-existent board UUID for filtering, call the PATCH endpoint to list topics with this board filter, and expect zero items in the data array.

Verify that role-based access control is enforced. Attempt to list board topics as a non-authenticated or suspended user. The response should return an error or filtered results per business rule. Prior to this, set up a suspended member using the appropriate suspension endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to then suspend for the restricted access test.
Suspend the member so they can be used to test access restrictions on listing topics.

scenario.draft: Verify successful retrieval of a board topic by its ID. Create a board, then create a topic under that board. Use the returned topic ID to fetch details with this GET endpoint and verify all fields match the creation data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board to attach the topic to.
Create a board topic and obtain its ID for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval with a randomly generated UUID that does not match any topic. The response should be a clear 404 or appropriate error indicating topic does not exist.

Verify that access-controlled or private topics are inaccessible to unauthorized users. Create a private or restricted topic, then attempt to access as an unauthorized or insufficient permission user, expecting a permission denied or not found error depending on configuration.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board.
Create a restricted board topic (e.g., private or staff-only).
Create a regular member for unauthorized access testing.

scenario.draft: Test successful board topic creation. Create a board, then use a member to post a new topic specifying unique code, title, and description. Validate that the response matches the input data and all required fields are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board to assign the new topic to.
Create a member to be the creator of the board topic.

scenario.draft: Test that creating a topic with a code or title already used in the same board fails as per uniqueness constraints. Set up a board and member, create the first topic, then attempt to create a second topic with duplicated code or title and expect a validation error or conflict response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board to use in topic creation tests.
Create a member to be the topic creator.
Create the initial topic to establish code/title uniqueness in the board.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a board topic omitting required fields (such as title, code, or board ID) and verify the API returns appropriate validation errors for each missing field.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board (for positive scenario controls as needed).
Create a member for the test context.

scenario.draft: Test that unauthenticated, non-member, or suspended users are prevented from creating a board topic. Attempt creation with each type and expect errors reflecting business rule enforcement (e.g., 403 for non-member, 403 or suitable error for suspended user).

dependencies.purpose: Create a board for the context.
Create a member to suspend.
Suspend the member to test for suspended user restriction.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing board topic's fields (such as title and description) by its creator or qualified roles. Create a board, member, and topic. Then, update with new values and verify the response reflects the changes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board for the topic.
Create a member to own the topic.
Create a topic to be updated.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a topic to use an already-taken code or title within the board, or to violate schema validation (such as empty title or too-long code). The API must reject the update and provide the correct validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board.
Create a member for topic creation.
Create two topics in the board to set up uniqueness violation scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a board topic by providing a random UUID that does not belong to any topic. The API should return a 404 or appropriate not found error.

Validate successful deletion (soft or hard) of a board topic by its creator, admin, or moderator. Create a board, topic, and ensure the creator or Staff role attempts the delete. Confirm the topic is no longer visible in listings but may be available for audit purposes if soft-deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board for the topic.
Create a member to own the topic.
Create the topic for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that users who are neither the topic creator nor have sufficient permissions (e.g., other members or unauthenticated users) cannot delete the topic. Attempt deletion using such users and verify a permission denied or forbidden error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board.
Create a member as the topic owner.
Create the topic tied to the owner member.
Create another non-owner member to attempt unauthorized deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a topic by providing a UUID which is not linked to any actual topic record. Expect the API to return a suitable 404 or not found error response.

Test listing notifications for an authenticated member with valid pagination and filter criteria. Set up a member with multiple notifications, and verify that the correct subset is returned according to the specified filters and paging preferences. Ensure that only notifications belonging to the logged-in member are accessible, and verify the pagination metadata in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member who will receive notifications.
Create multiple notification entries for the newly registered member.

scenario.draft: Test that access is denied when attempting to list notifications as an unauthenticated user or while trying to view another member's notifications using forged or tampered authentication. Confirm that only the authenticated member can access their own notifications.

Test retrieving full notification details for a specific notification that belongs to the authenticated member. First, create a member and at least one notification for that member. Then, fetch the notification by ID and verify all expected fields are present, including delivery and read status.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a member who will receive notifications.
Create a notification for the member.

scenario.draft: Test that requesting notification details for a notification not belonging to the authenticated member returns a 403 forbidden or similar error. This ensures privacy boundaries between members are strictly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members: one will receive the notification, the other will act as the unauthorized accessor.
Issue a notification to one member, then attempt to access it using the other member's credentials.

scenario.draft: Test error response when trying to retrieve a notification using an invalid or non-existent notification ID. Confirm that the response is a 404 not found or appropriate error, validating correct ID parsing and error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to act as the requester.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated member can successfully create a notification for themselves by providing all required fields. Ensure the notification is returned with the correct contents, and verify audit logging requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Register the member who will create and receive the notification.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin or moderator can create a notification for another member. This requires creating both an admin and a member account, then authenticating as the admin to issue a notification to the member. Validate that the notification is delivered only to the intended recipient, and that the system records proper audit information.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member who will receive the notification.
Create and promote a member to admin for notification creation rights.

scenario.draft: Test various invalid cases for creating notifications, such as omitting required fields (title, type, body, recipient, etc.) or attempting creation by an unauthorized or unauthenticated user. Confirm that proper error codes and messages are returned, and that no notification is created.

dependencies.purpose: Register one or more members to test failure scenarios with missing fields or missing authentication.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can mark their own notification as read by updating the read_at property. First, create a member and issue a notification. Then, perform the update and verify the notification status changes to 'read' for that member only.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will receive a notification.
Issue a notification to the member.

scenario.draft: Test that a member cannot update another member's notification (e.g., mark as read or alter content). Create two members, let one receive a notification, and attempt an update as the other. Confirm that a 403 error or equivalent is returned, and that no changes occur.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members, one as the notification owner and the other as a non-owner.
Create a notification for the owner member.

scenario.draft: Test update failure when providing an invalid notification ID or malformed/invalid payload (e.g., missing required fields or setting forbidden fields). Confirm that error handling returns a 404 for missing records and proper validation errors for bad input.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a member for negative testing.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can successfully delete one of their own notifications. First, create a member and notification, then delete and verify the deletion confirmation and that the notification no longer appears in the member's notification list.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to own the notification.
Add a notification to be deleted by the owner.

scenario.draft: Test that a member or moderator cannot delete another member's notification, ensuring permissions are respected. Attempt to delete as a non-owner and confirm a 403 error is returned. Verify that the notification remains accessible to its true owner.

dependencies.purpose: Set up two members, one as notification owner and another as non-owner.
Create a notification for the owner member.

scenario.draft: Test the error response for attempting to delete a notification using an invalid or non-existent ID. Ensure the system returns a 404 not found or appropriate error with no changes to data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for negative deletion test cases.

scenario.draft: Test listing posts with valid search filters, thread ID, and pagination options. First, create a member and a thread, then create several posts under the thread using the POST /discussionboard/threads/posts endpoint. Submit a PATCH /discussionboard/threads/posts request with filters for that thread and specify pagination parameters (e.g., page size, sort order). Expect the response to include only posts from the specified thread, with correct metadata and pagination. This reflects a typical forum browse/use case.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new board member who will author posts.
Create a discussion thread in which posts will be created.
Create multiple posts within the thread to set up filter and pagination tests.

scenario.draft: Test that searching for posts of a non-existent thread (invalid thread ID in search filter) yields an empty data set or suitable error. No posts are created for this thread, and the PATCH /discussionboard/threads/posts endpoint should gracefully handle this situation without error, returning zero results.

Create a member, suspend the member using POST /discussionboard/actors/memberSuspensions, and attempt to list posts via PATCH /discussionboard/threads/posts. The API should enforce suspension-based restrictions and return a permission error or filtered/empty data as per system policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to be suspended.
Suspend the member prior to the attempt to list posts.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving detailed post information by a valid post ID. This involves registering a member, creating a thread, then creating a post in that thread, and finally retrieving the post with GET /discussionboard/threads/posts/{id}. The returned data should match the created post including author, content, and timestamps.

dependencies.purpose: To create a member who will author the post.
